title: Dirac scattering and the non-linear Fourier transform
summary: Carathéodory linear systems with integrable coefficients and a holomorphic parameter; half-plane function theory (Poisson integrals, Fatou, bounded holomorphic functions, H², Paley–Wiener, outer functions); Dirac systems with locally integrable complex potential, their fundamental matrix and Hermite–Biehler functions; finite-interval SU(1,1) scattering with the half-plane inequality, outerness and the non-linear Plancherel identity (constant π/2); the square-integrable scattering limit and the non-linear Fourier transform with boundary values, Plancherel at infinity and L² convergence of truncations; de Branges spaces, Weyl functions, spectral measures and the Szegő condition; meromorphic inner functions and resonances; universality and approximation of Hermite–Biehler functions; subinterval scattering data, the time resonances spend near a point, resonance-free points, and the pointwise convergence of the non-linear Fourier transform at almost every resonance-free point for real square-integrable potentials (the conditional form of Poltoratski's theorem).

layers.title: Carathéodory linear systems with a holomorphic parameter

targets.name: le_mul_exp_integral_of_le_add_integral
targets.statement: Let `a ≤ b`, let `β : ℝ → ℝ` be nonnegative and integrable on `[a, b]`, let `α ∈ ℝ`, and let `u : ℝ → ℝ` be measurable and bounded on `[a, b]` with `u(t) ≤ α + ∫ₐᵗ β u` for every `t ∈ [a, b]`. Prove that `u(t) ≤ α exp(∫ₐᵗ β)` for every `t ∈ [a, b]`, and the backward form on `[a, b]` with `∫ₜᵇ`. Route: `v(t) = ∫ₐᵗ β u` is absolutely continuous with `v′ = βu ≤ αβ + βv` almost everywhere, so `(v e^{−∫ₐᵗβ})′ ≤ αβ e^{−∫ₐᵗβ}` almost everywhere; integrate with the constancy theorem (coddingtonlevinson1955, Ch. 1, waived; the constant-kernel case is Tau Ceti `TauCeti.le_mul_exp_of_le_add_mul_integral`).

locator.where: Ch. 1 (Grönwall's inequality), waived; constant-kernel case Tau Ceti TauCeti.le_mul_exp_of_le_add_mul_integral

targets.name: existsUnique_caratheodory_linear
targets.statement: Let `a ≤ b`, `t₀ ∈ [a, b]`, `y₀ ∈ E`, let `P` be a coefficient on `[a, b]` and let `F : ℝ → E` be integrable on `[a, b]`. Prove that there is a `Y : ℝ → E`, continuous on `[a, b]`, with `Y(t) = y₀ + ∫_{t₀}^{t} (P(s)Y(s) + F(s)) ds` for every `t ∈ [a, b]`, and that any two such functions agree on `[a, b]`. Prove that every such `Y` is absolutely continuous on `[a, b]`, has derivative `P(t)Y(t) + F(t)` at almost every `t ∈ (a, b)`, and satisfies `‖Y(t)‖ ≤ (‖y₀‖ + |∫_{t₀}^{t} ‖F‖|) exp|∫_{t₀}^{t} ‖P‖|` for `t ∈ [a, b]`; conversely a `Y` that is absolutely continuous on `[a, b]` with `Y(t₀) = y₀` and derivative `P Y + F` at almost every `t ∈ (a, b)` agrees on `[a, b]` with these solutions. Route: Picard iteration in `C([a, b], E)`, where the `n`-th iterate moves two curves at time `t` by at most `(∫_{t₀}^{t}‖P‖)ⁿ/n!` times their distance, so that some iterate is a contraction; uniqueness by 1.1 (coddingtonlevinson1955, Ch. 2 §1, waived; romanov2014 line 212–224 for the canonical-system case).
hypotheses: P a.e. strongly measurable with ‖P‖ integrable on [a,b]

tests.name: zeroData

tests.statement: Agreement with Tau Ceti: for `𝕜 = ℝ` and essentially bounded `P`, the solution is the one of `TauCeti.exists_continuousOn_eq_forall_mem_Icc_eq_picard`, by `TauCeti.eqOn_of_forall_mem_Icc_eq_picard`.

tests.name: fixedParameterOnC2
tests.statement: Fixed parameter on `ℂ²`: for `E = EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 2)`, `F = 0` and `P(t) = Ω(λ − V(t))` with `V` Hermitian and integrable on `[a, b]`, the theorem is the local integral-equation existence and uniqueness of OperatorTheory/UnboundedOperators §4.8 for `Ju′ + Vu = λu`. For `V = 0`, `λ = −z` and `t₀ = 0` the solutions from `(1, 0)` and `(0, 1)` are the columns of `[[cos tz, −sin tz], [sin tz, cos tz]]`, the free fundamental matrix of §3.1; the sign `λ = z` gives the transpose `[[cos tz, sin tz], [−sin tz, cos tz]]`.

They agree on `[0, 1]` and differ at `5/2`, so a uniqueness claim for functions on all of `ℝ` is false.

targets.name: det_caratheodoryPropagator
targets.statement: For `E = Fin n → 𝕜` or `E = EuclideanSpace 𝕜 (Fin n)` and a matrix coefficient `P`, prove `det N_P(t, s) = exp(∫_s^t tr P)` for `s, t ∈ I`, with `N_P(t, s)` and `P(r)` identified with their matrices in the standard basis (coddingtonlevinson1955, Ch. 1 §7, waived; romanov2014 line 218–219 for `det ≡ 1`). Route: fix `s`. At almost every `t` the curve `N_P(·, s)` has derivative `P(t)N` at `t`, where `N = N_P(t, s)` is invertible (§1.2, §1.3). The chain rule and Jacobi's formula at an invertible matrix (Tau Ceti `Matrix.hasFDerivAt_det`, restricted to real scalars when `𝕜 = ℂ`) then give `∂ₜ det N_P(t, s) = det N · tr(N⁻¹P(t)N) = det N · tr P(t)`. Each entry `N ↦ (N e_j)_i` is `1`-Lipschitz on `E →L[𝕜] E`, since `|(N e_j)_i| ≤ ‖N e_j‖ ≤ ‖N‖`. So the entries of the absolutely continuous curve `N_P(·, s)` (§1.2) are absolutely continuous (Mathlib `LipschitzWith.comp_absolutelyContinuousOnInterval`). The function `det N_P(·, s)` is then absolutely continuous, being a finite sum of products of these entries (the Leibniz expansion). It is therefore an absolutely continuous solution of the scalar equation `y′ = (tr P) y`, `y(s) = 1`, whose coefficient is integrable because `|tr P| ≤ n‖P‖`. By the uniqueness clause of §1.2 it equals `exp(∫_s^t tr P)`, which solves the same equation. The same formula holds for `E = EuclideanSpace 𝕜 (Fin n)`, the carrier of §3.1. Mathlib's `EuclideanSpace.equiv` is a continuous linear equivalence with `Fin n → 𝕜` that is the identity on coordinates. Conjugation by it carries a coefficient to a coefficient, and so, by the uniqueness clause of §1.2, the propagator to the propagator. It changes neither the matrices in the standard basis nor their determinants and traces.
hypotheses: E = Fin n → 𝕜 or E = EuclideanSpace 𝕜 (Fin n)
P a matrix coefficient on I

tests.name: agreementWithTauCetiDetExp

targets.name: differentiableOn_caratheodoryPropagator
targets.statement: Let `E` be a complex Banach space, `U ⊆ ℂ` open, and `P : ℝ × ℂ → (E →L[ℂ] E)` such that `t ↦ P(t, z)` is a coefficient on `I` for each `z ∈ U`, `z ↦ P(t, z)` is holomorphic on `U` for almost every `t ∈ I`, and for every compact `K ⊆ U` there is `m_K` integrable on compact subintervals of `I` with `‖P(t, z)‖ ≤ m_K(t)` for `z ∈ K` and almost every `t`. Prove that for `s, t ∈ I` the map `z ↦ N_{P(·,z)}(t, s)` is holomorphic on `U`, that `(t, s, z) ↦ N_{P(·,z)}(t, s)` is continuous on `I × I × U`, that `z ↦ N_{P(·,z)}(·, s)` is holomorphic from `U` into `C(J, E →L[ℂ] E)` for every compact `J ⊆ I`, with `‖N_{P(·,z)}(t, s)‖ ≤ exp|∫_s^t m_K|` for `z ∈ K`, and that `∂_z N(t, s) = ∫_s^t N(t, r) ∂_z P(r, z) N(r, s) dr`. In particular an entire coefficient (`U = ℂ`) gives entire propagators (romanov2014 line 220–222; coddingtonlevinson1955, Ch. 1 §7, waived). Route: each Dyson term is a parametric integral of a holomorphic integrand dominated on compacts, hence holomorphic, and the series converges locally uniformly.
hypotheses: t ↦ P(t,z) a coefficient for z ∈ U
z ↦ P(t,z) holomorphic for a.e. t
locally uniform integrable domination on compacts K ⊆ U

tests.statement: The domination hypothesis is needed: `E = ℂ`, `I = [0, 1]`, `P(t, z) = 1/(z − t)`, `N(t, 0) = z/(z − t)` is holomorphic on `U = {Re z > 2}` where the bound holds, and has a pole at `z = t` for every `t ∈ (0, 1]`, so no statement on a `U` meeting `[0, 1]` holds.

tests.name: theDiracCoefficientIs
tests.statement: The Dirac coefficient `P(t, z) = −Ω(z − Q_q(t)) = [[f(t), −z − g(t)], [z − g(t), −f(t)]]` on `EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 2)` is entire with `m_K(t) = sup_K |z| + |q(t)|` in the Euclidean operator norm. In the maximum-row-sum norm of `Fin 2 → ℂ` the coefficient at `z = 0` has norm `|f(t)| + |g(t)|`, which exceeds `|q(t)|` whenever `f(t)g(t) ≠ 0`: for `q = 1 + i` it is `2 > √2 = |q|`. At a fixed `z` the conclusion is the fixed-parameter existence statement of 1.2.

targets.name: existsUnique_caratheodory
targets.statement: Let `t₀ ∈ I`, `x₀ ∈ E` and `F : ℝ × E → E` with `t ↦ F(t, x)` strongly measurable on `I` for each `x`, `‖F(t, x) − F(t, y)‖ ≤ L(t)‖x − y‖` and `‖F(t, x₀)‖ ≤ m(t)` for almost every `t ∈ I` and all `x, y`, where `L, m ≥ 0` are integrable on compact subintervals of `I`. Prove that there is a `Y : ℝ → E`, continuous on `I`, with `Y(t) = x₀ + ∫_{t₀}^{t} F(s, Y(s)) ds` for `t ∈ I`, and that any two such functions agree on `I`; that every such `Y` is absolutely continuous on compact subintervals of `I` with `‖Y(t) − x₀‖ ≤ |∫_{t₀}^{t} m| exp|∫_{t₀}^{t} L|`; and that two initial values give solutions at distance at most `‖x₀ − x₀′‖ exp|∫_{t₀}^{t} L|` at every `t ∈ I`. Prove the local form. Let `B` be the closed ball of radius `r` about `x₀`, suppose the two bounds hold only for `x, y ∈ B` and almost every `t ∈ [t₀, t₀ + δ] ⊆ I`, and let `τ ≤ δ` satisfy `(∫_{t₀}^{t₀+τ} m) exp(∫_{t₀}^{t₀+τ} L) ≤ r`. Call a solution on `[t₀, t₀ + τ]` a `Y` continuous there with `s ↦ F(s, Y(s))` integrable on `[t₀, t₀ + τ]` and the integral equation for `t ∈ [t₀, t₀ + τ]`. Then there is a solution on `[t₀, t₀ + τ]` with values in `B`, and any two solutions with values in `B` agree on `[t₀, t₀ + τ]`. If the inequality is strict, every solution on `[t₀, t₀ + τ]` has values in `B`, so any two solutions agree there: a solution leaving `B` meets the sphere `‖x − x₀‖ = r` at a first time `t*`, and 1.1 on `[t₀, t*]` bounds `‖Y(t*) − x₀‖` by `(∫_{t₀}^{t₀+τ} m) exp(∫_{t₀}^{t₀+τ} L) < r`. The composite `s ↦ F(s, Y(s))` is almost everywhere strongly measurable for every continuous `Y`, and in the local form for every continuous `Y` with values in `B`: after `F(t, ·)` is replaced by `0` for the `t` of a null set outside which the Lipschitz bound holds, every `F(t, ·)` is continuous on `E` (on `B` in the local form) and every section `t ↦ F(t, x)` is unchanged almost everywhere, so Tau Ceti `MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable.apply_of_forall_of_continuous` applies with the parameter space `E` (the ball `B`) (coddingtonlevinson1955, Ch. 2 §1, waived).
hypotheses: L, m ≥ 0 locally integrable on I

local form: the bounds for x, y in the closed ball B of radius r about x₀ and a.e. t ∈ [t₀, t₀+δ], and (∫m)exp(∫L) ≤ r over [t₀, t₀+τ]; uniqueness among B-valued solutions, among all solutions when the inequality is strict

On the ball of radius `r = 1` the local bounds are `L = 2(1 + r) = 4` and `m = 1`, and `τ = 0.1` satisfies `τ e^{4τ} ≈ 0.149 ≤ 1`; the local form gives the solution on `[0, 0.1]`, where indeed `1/(1 − t) ≤ 1.12` stays in the ball.

tests.statement: The local uniqueness clause needs the ball or the strict inequality: `E = ℝ`, `I = [0, 2]`, `t₀ = 0`, `x₀ = 0`, `r = 1`, `δ = τ = 2`, `F(t, x) = 1` for `t < 1` and `F(t, x) = 2√(max(x − 1, 0))` for `t ≥ 1`. On `B = [−1, 1]` the bounds hold with `L = 0` and `m = 1_{[0, 1)}`, and `(∫₀² m) e⁰ = 1 = r`. Both `min(t, 1)` and the function equal to `t` on `[0, 1]` and to `1 + (t − 1)²` on `[1, 2]` solve the equation on `[0, 2]`; the second leaves `B` after `t = 1`. For `τ < 1` the inequality is strict and `Y(t) = t` is the only solution on `[0, τ]`.

layers.title: Function theory of the upper half-plane

targets.name: poissonIntegral
targets.statement: Define the Poisson kernel `P(z, x)` for `z ∈ ℂ₊`, `x ∈ ℝ` as Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.halfSpacePoissonKernel 2 v` with unit inward normal `v = (0, 1)`, pole `z` and boundary point `x`, read through Mathlib's `Complex.orthonormalBasisOneI`; since `⟨v, z⟩ = Im z` and `2ω₂ = 2π` (Mathlib `EuclideanSpace.volume_ball_fin_two`), it is `P(z, x) = Im z/(π|x − z|²)`, the notation used below. Define the Poisson measure `Π = dx/(1 + x²)`; a positive Borel measure `ν` on `ℝ` is Poisson-finite when `∫ dν/(1 + x²) < ∞`. Define the Poisson integral `P[ν](z) = ∫ P(z, x) dν(x)`, and for a complex `h ∈ L¹(Π)` write `P[h] = P[h dx]` (componentwise). For a Poisson-finite `ν` (or a real `h ∈ L¹(Π)`) define the Schwarz integral `S[ν](z) = (1/(πi)) ∫ (1/(x − z) − x/(1 + x²)) dν(x)`, and for `h ∈ L¹(ℝ)` the integral normalised at infinity `S⁰[h](z) = (1/(πi)) ∫ h(x)/(x − z) dx` (poltoratski2024 line 250–254 and 610–614; mauth2022 line 378–392).
hypotheses: ν a Poisson-finite positive Borel measure on ℝ (or h ∈ L¹(Π))

locator.where: line 250–254 and 610–614; mauth2022 line 378–392, Lemma 3 line 390–392

api.name: andWithSoIs
api.statement: `∫ P(z, x) dx = 1` (Tau Ceti `TauCeti.integral_halfSpacePoissonKernel`; the hyperplane carries the Lebesgue measure of `ℝ` by Mathlib `LinearIsometryEquiv.measurePreserving`), and `P(z, x) ≤ C(z)/(1 + x²)` with `C(z) = 2(1 + (Re z)²) max(Im z, 1/Im z)/π`, so `P[ν]` is finite on `ℂ₊` for Poisson-finite `ν`.

api.name: isHarmonicOnNonnegative
api.statement: `P[ν]` is harmonic on `ℂ₊` (mauth2022 Lemma 3 line 390–392), nonnegative, and `P[ν] = Re S[ν]`; `S[ν]` is holomorphic on `ℂ₊` and real at `z = i`; `S⁰[h] − S[h]` is the imaginary constant `−(i/π) ∫ x h(x)/(1 + x²) dx`. Route: on a compact subset of `ℂ₊` the `z`-derivative `(x − z)^{−2}` of the Schwarz integrand is bounded by a constant times `1/(1 + x²)`, so `S[ν]` is holomorphic (Mathlib `hasFDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_of_fderiv_le`), hence analytic (Mathlib `DifferentiableOn.analyticAt`). Its real part `P[ν]` is then harmonic (Mathlib `AnalyticAt.harmonicAt_re`). It is nonnegative because the kernel is positive (Tau Ceti `TauCeti.halfSpacePoissonKernel_pos`).

api.name: soExactlyWhen
api.statement: `P(i, x) = 1/(π(1 + x²))`, so `h ∈ L¹(Π)` exactly when `P[|h|](i) < ∞`.

api.name: cayleyComparisonWithAnd
api.statement: Cayley comparison: with `w = (z − i)/(z + i)` and `ζ = (x − i)/(x + i)`, `P(z, x) = poissonKernel 0 w ζ · 1/(π(1 + x²))`, where Mathlib's disc Poisson kernel is `poissonKernel 0 w ζ = (1 − |w|²)/|ζ − w|²` for `|ζ| = 1`. So `P[ν](z) = ∫ poissonKernel 0 w ζ dσ(ζ)` is the disc Poisson integral at `w` of the image `σ` of `dν/(π(1 + x²))` under Tau Ceti `TauCeti.boundaryCayley`.

api.name: translationAndDilationCovariance
api.statement: Translation and dilation covariance: for the translate `ν_u` of `ν` by `u ∈ ℝ`, `P[ν_u](z) = P[ν](z − u)`; for `λ > 0` and the image `ν^λ` of `ν` under `x ↦ x/λ`, `P[ν^λ](z) = λ P[ν](λz)`.

tests.name: identificationWithThePinnedKernel
tests.statement: Identification with the pinned kernel: at `z = 1 + i` and `x = 3`, Tau Ceti's kernel at `n = 2`, `v = (0, 1)`, with pole `z` is `2 · 1/(2π · 5) = 1/(5π)`, which is `Im z/(π|x − z|²)`. With the two arguments exchanged (pole `x`) it is `0`, because `⟨v, x⟩ = 0` for real `x`.

tests.name: lebesgueMeasureAKernel
tests.statement: Lebesgue measure: `P[dx] ≡ 1`; a kernel without the factor `1/π` would give `π`.

tests.name: withValueAt
tests.statement: `ν = δ₀`: `P[δ₀](z) = Im z/(π|z|²) = Im(−1/(πz))`, with value `1/π` at `z = i`. It is harmonic on `ℂ₊`, as Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_halfSpacePoissonKernel_left` states for the kernel in its pole.

tests.name: andAtTheDirect
tests.statement: `h = 1/(1 + x²)`: `P[h](z) = Re(i/(z + i))` and `S[h](z) = i/(z + i)`; at `z = 2i`, the direct integral `(2/π)∫ dx/((x² + 4)(x² + 1)) = 1/3 = i/(3i)`. This `h` is real, bounded and continuous, so `P[h]` is also Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.halfSpacePoissonIntegral` at `n = 2`, harmonic by `TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_halfSpacePoissonIntegral`.

tests.name: cayleyComparisonWithMathlibPoissonKernel
tests.statement: Cayley comparison at `z = 2i`, `x = 1`: `w = 1/3`, `ζ = −i`, `poissonKernel 0 (1/3) (−i) = (8/9)/(10/9) = 4/5` and `(4/5)/(2π) = 2/(5π) = P(2i, 1)`. For `h(x) = (x² − 1)/(x² + 1) = Re ζ`, Mathlib's Poisson formula on the unit disc (`InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd.circleAverage_poissonKernel_smul` for the harmonic function `Re`) gives `P[h](z) = Re w`. At `z = 2i` the direct integral is `(2/π)∫ (x² − 1)/((x² + 1)(x² + 4)) dx = 1/3 = Re(1/3)`. A kernel that also carried the circle-average factor `1/(2π)` would give `1/(6π)`.

tests.name: isNotPoissonFinite
tests.statement: `ν = |x| dx` is not Poisson-finite (`∫ |x|/(1 + x²) = ∞`) and `P[ν] ≡ ∞`.

targets.name: exists_eq_mul_im_add_poissonIntegral
targets.statement: Prove that a nonnegative harmonic `u` on `ℂ₊` is `u(z) = c Im z + P[ν](z)` for a unique `c ≥ 0` and a unique Poisson-finite `ν`, that `πy u(iy) − πc y² = ∫ y²/(x² + y²) dν(x)` increases to `ν(ℝ)` as `y → ∞`, that `c = lim u(iy)/y` as `y → ∞`, and that `ν` is the vague limit of the measures `u(x + iy) dx` as `y → 0` (garnett2007, Ch. I §3, uncertified). This is the harmonic form of the Herglotz representation of AutomorphicSpectralTheory §0.5: if `F` is holomorphic on `ℂ₊` with `Im F = u` and `(a, b, ν_F)` is its triple there, then `c = b` and `ν = πν_F`, because `Im (x − z)⁻¹ = π P(z, x)`. Route: the function `i(∂ₓu − i∂ᵧu)`, `i` times the complex partial of `u`, is holomorphic on `ℂ₊` by Mathlib's `HarmonicAt.differentiableAt_complex_partial`; it has a primitive by Tau Ceti `DifferentiableOn.hasDerivAt_wedgeIntegral_upperHalfPlane`, whose imaginary part has the gradient of `u`, so after subtracting an imaginary constant the primitive is an `F` with `Im F = u` and `F′ = i(∂ₓu − i∂ᵧu)`, and §0.5 applies to it. Uniqueness: for each representation, `cz + (1/π)∫ ((x − z)⁻¹ − x/(1 + x²)) dν(x)` is holomorphic with imaginary part `u` and real part `0` at `i`; two holomorphic functions on `ℂ₊` with the same imaginary part differ by a real constant, so the two functions coincide and the uniqueness of the triple in §0.5 gives that of `(c, ν)`. Mass: `πy P[ν](iy)` is `∫ y²/(x² + y²) dν(x)`, which increases to `ν(ℝ)` by monotone convergence, and `P[ν](iy)/y → 0`. Vague limit: for `φ` continuous with compact support, `∫ φ(x) P[ν](x + iy) dx = ∫ (∫ P(x + iy, t) φ(x) dx) dν(t)` by Tonelli, the inner integral tends to `φ(t)` with a bound `C_φ/(1 + t²)` for `y ≤ 1`, and the term `cy ∫ φ` tends to `0`.

tests.name: item0
tests.statement: `u = Im z`: `c = 1`, `ν = 0`. The complex partial of `u` is `∂ₓu − i∂ᵧu = −i`, and `F′ = i · (−i) = 1` is the derivative of `F = z`; the conjugate partial `∂ₓu + i∂ᵧu = i` is not `F′`.

tests.name: andForEvery
tests.statement: `u = P[δ₀]`: `c = 0`, `ν = δ₀`, and `πy u(iy) = 1 = ν(ℝ)` for every `y`. Here `F = −1/(πz)` has the triple `(0, 0, δ₀/π)` of AutomorphicSpectralTheory §0.5, and `ν = π · δ₀/π = δ₀`; reading `ν = ν_F` would give mass `1/π`, while `πy u(iy) = 1`. The derivative `F′ = 1/(πz²)` equals `i(∂ₓu − i∂ᵧu)` with `∂ₓu − i∂ᵧu = −i/(πz²)`.

tests.name: and
tests.statement: `u ≡ 1 = P[dx]`: `ν(ℝ) = ∞` and `πy u(iy) = πy → ∞`.

tests.name: isHarmonicButTakes
tests.statement: `u = Re z` is harmonic but takes the value `−1` at `−1 + i`; positivity is a hypothesis.

targets.name: nontangentialMaximal
targets.statement: For `x ∈ ℝ` and `0 < h ≤ ∞` define the cone `Γ_h(x) = {z ∈ ℂ₊ : |Re z − x| < Im z < h}` and, for `u : ℂ₊ → ℂ`, the nontangential maximal function `M_h u(x) = sup_{z ∈ Γ_h(x)} |u(z)|` with values in `[0, ∞]`. A function has nontangential limit `L` at `x` when it tends to `L` along the filter of `Γ_∞(x)` at `x` (poltoratski2024 line 615–622; mauth2022 line 411–420; garnett2007, Ch. I §§4–5, pp. 27, 55–56, uncertified). Its API:
hypotheses: h ∈ L¹(Π) (bounded-cone bounds), g ∈ L²(ℝ) (L² bound)

locator.where: Lemmas 5–6, Corollary 1, line 411–433; poltoratski2024 line 615–622; garnett2007 Ch. I §§4–5 (uncertified)

api.name: coneComparisonForAnd
api.statement: Cone comparison: for `x′ + iy ∈ Γ_∞(x)` and every `s ∈ ℝ`, `P(x′ + iy, s) ≤ 3 P(x + iy, s)`; hence for `g` locally integrable with `P[|g|]` finite, `M_∞ P[g](x) ≤ 3 · TauCeti.maximalFunction volume g x`. The kernel inequality is Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.halfSpacePoissonKernel_le_mul` at `n = 2` with the poles `x′ + iy` and `x + iy` of equal height and `A = √3`, so that `Aⁿ = 3`.

api.name: apertureIndependenceConesGive
api.statement: Aperture independence: cones `|Re z − x| < α Im z`, `α > 0`, give the same nontangential limits, by the same comparison with `A² = max(2, 1 + 2α²)`, which is `3` for `α = 1`.

api.name: localisationForAndThere
api.statement: Localisation: for `h ∈ L¹(Π)` and `R > 0` there is `C_R`, depending only on `R`, with `M_1 P[h](x) ≤ 3 · TauCeti.maximalFunction volume (h · 1_{[−R−2, R+2]}) x + C_R ‖h‖_{L¹(Π)}` for `|x| ≤ R`.

api.name: weakTypeForSo
api.statement: Weak type: `|{x ∈ [−R, R] : M_1 P[h](x) > λ}| ≤ C_R ‖h‖_{L¹(Π)}/λ` for `λ > 0`, so `√(M_1 P[|h|])` is integrable on every bounded interval (mauth2022 Lemma 5 and Corollary 1, line 421–427).

api.name: strongTypeForWith
api.statement: Strong type: `‖M_∞ P[g]‖_{L²} ≤ C‖g‖_{L²}` for `g ∈ L²(ℝ)` with an absolute constant `C` (mauth2022 Lemma 6 line 430).

api.name: routeGivesIsRadially
api.statement: Route: `|s − x| ≤ |s − x′| + y` gives `(s − x)² + y² ≤ 3((s − x′)² + y²)`, which is the distance hypothesis `|s − (x + iy)| ≤ √3 |s − (x′ + iy)|` of the pinned comparison. `P(x + iy, ·)` is radially decreasing about `x` with integral `1` (§2.1), so its integral against `|g|` is at most the maximal function by the layer-cake formula; then Tau Ceti's weak and strong type bounds.

tests.name: andWhileTheMaximal
tests.statement: `h = 1_{[0,1]}` and `x = 2`: `P[h](2 + i) = (arctan 2 − π/4)/π ≈ 0.102`, while the maximal function of `h` at `2` is `1/4` (attained at radius `2`), and `0.102 ≤ 3 · 1/4`.

tests.name: theConstantAtAnd
tests.statement: The constant `3`: at `x = 0`, `z = 0.99 + i ∈ Γ_∞(0)` and `s = 1`, `P(0.99 + i, 1) = 1/(1.0001π)` and `3P(i, 1) = 3/(2π)`, so the inequality holds; at `s = 2` the ratio is `P(0.99 + i, 2)/P(i, 2) = 5/2.0201 ≈ 2.475`. Over the open cone the ratio `P(x′ + iy, s)/P(iy, s)` has supremum `(s² + y²)/((s − y)² + y²)` for `s ≥ y`, largest at `s = y(1 + √5)/2` with value `((1 + √5)/2)² ≈ 2.618`, not attained; so no constant below `2.618` works, and `3` is not sharp. The point `1 + i` lies on the boundary of `Γ_∞(0)`, not in it.

tests.name: bothMaximalFunctionsVanish
tests.statement: `h = 0`: both maximal functions vanish; `h ≡ 1` (in `L¹(Π)`, not in `L¹`): `P[h] ≡ 1` and `M_1 P[h] ≡ 1`.

tests.name: theGlobalMaximalFunction
tests.statement: The global maximal function of `h ∈ L¹(Π)` can be infinite (for `h ≡ 1` the averages over `B(x, r)` stay `1`, but for `h(x) = |x|^{1/2}` they grow like `√r`), which is why the bound is localised to `[−R − 2, R + 2]` with a tail term.

targets.name: ae_tendsto_poissonIntegral_nontangential
targets.statement: Let `ν` be Poisson-finite with Lebesgue decomposition `ν = w dx + ν_s`. Prove that for almost every `x ∈ ℝ`, `P[ν](z) → w(x)` as `z → x` nontangentially; in particular `P[ν_s] → 0` nontangentially almost everywhere, and `P[h] → h(x)` nontangentially at almost every `x` for complex `h ∈ L¹(Π)` (mauth2022 Lemmas 4 and 7, line 404–436; garnett2007, Ch. I §§3–5, pp. 16, 30, uncertified). Route: at a Lebesgue point of `w` where `ν_s(B(x, r))/2r → 0` (Mathlib `VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div` and `VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv`), split `ν − w(x)dx` near and far from `x` and use the cone domination of §2.3.
hypotheses: ν Poisson-finite with Lebesgue decomposition w dx + ν_s

locator.where: Lemmas 4 and 7, line 404–436; garnett2007 Ch. I §§3–5 pp. 16, 30 (uncertified)

tests.name: theLimitIsAt
tests.statement: `ν = δ₀`: the limit is `0` at every `x ≠ 0`, and `w = 0`.

tests.name: theLimitIsOn
tests.statement: `h = 1_{[0,1]}`: the limit is `1` on `(0, 1)` and `0` off `[0, 1]`; at the jump `x = 0` there is no nontangential limit, since `P[h](iy) → 1/2` while `P[h](−y/2 + iy) → 1/2 − arctan(1/2)/π ≈ 0.352`.

tests.name: continuousBoundedTheLimit
tests.statement: Continuous bounded `h`: the limit exists at every point and equals `h(x)`, even without restriction on the approach; this is Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.tendsto_halfSpacePoissonIntegral` at `n = 2`, applied to `Re h` and `Im h`.

targets.name: boundaryFunction
targets.statement: For `F` holomorphic and bounded on `ℂ₊` define its boundary function `F* ∈ L^∞(ℝ)` as the nontangential limit of `F`, which exists almost everywhere (garnett2007, Ch. II §§1–4, pp. 55, 64, uncertified). Its API:
hypotheses: F holomorphic and bounded on ℂ₊

api.name: andOnIsLinear
api.statement: `‖F*‖_∞ ≤ sup_{ℂ₊} |F|` and `F = P[F*]` on `ℂ₊`; `F ↦ F*` is linear and multiplicative.

api.name: ifExtendsContinuouslyTo
api.statement: If `F` extends continuously to the closed half-plane then `F* = F` on `ℝ`.

api.name: uniquenessIfVanishesOn
api.statement: Uniqueness: if `F*` vanishes on a set of positive measure then `F ≡ 0`.

api.name: ifThenAndOn
api.statement: If `F ≢ 0` then `log|F*| ∈ L¹(Π)` and `log|F(z)| ≤ P[log|F*|](z)` on `ℂ₊`.

api.name: routeTheBoundedFunctions
api.statement: Route: the bounded functions `F(· + iε)` are continuous up to `ℝ`. The Poisson integral of their restriction to `ℝ` is harmonic and tends to `F(x + iε)` at every `x ∈ ℝ` (Tau Ceti `TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_halfSpacePoissonIntegral` and `TauCeti.tendsto_halfSpacePoissonIntegral`, for the real and imaginary parts). So `F(· + iε) − P[F(· + iε)|_ℝ]`, reflected oddly across `ℝ`, is continuous, has the mean-value property (Tau Ceti `TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_of_setAverage_ball_eq`) and is bounded, hence constant by `InnerProductSpace.bounded_harmonic_on_complex_plane_is_constant`, hence `0`. A weak-* limit point of `F(· + iε)` in `L^∞(Π) = L¹(Π)^*` gives the Poisson representation, because `x ↦ (1 + x²)P(z, x)` is bounded and so lies in `L¹(Π)`; as a space of classes `L^∞(Π)` is `L^∞(ℝ)`, since `Π` and Lebesgue measure have the same null sets. §2.4 then gives the nontangential limits. Uniqueness and the logarithmic bound transport Tau Ceti `TauCeti.eqOn_const_ball_of_tendsto_circleMap` and `AnalyticOnNhd.le_circleAverage_log_norm` through the Cayley transform, under which a disc radius ending at `ζ ≠ 1` becomes an arc ending at `x` inside every cone at `x`. Jensen's bound is stated at the centre of the disc. It gives the logarithmic bound at `z = i`, because the Cayley transform carries `P(i, x) dx` to `dθ/(2π)`: this is §2.1's Cayley comparison at `w = 0`, where `poissonKernel 0 0 ζ = 1`. §2.1's translation and dilation covariance, applied to `F(Re z + (Im z) ·)`, then give the bound at every `z ∈ ℂ₊`.

tests.name: isBoundedByNot
tests.statement: `F(z) = e^{−i/z}` is bounded by `1` (`|F| = e^{−Im z/|z|²}`), not continuous at `0`, and `F* = e^{−i/x}` still has `P[F*] = F`.

targets.name: HardySpaceUpper
targets.statement: Define `H²(ℂ₊)` as the holomorphic `F` on `ℂ₊` with `‖F‖² = sup_{y>0} ∫ |F(x + iy)|² dx < ∞` (mauth2022 line 337–358). Its API:

locator.where: line 337–358, Lemmas 1, 2, 6, 9, 11; garnett2007 p. 84 and Ch. II §4 (uncertified)

api.name: boundaryValuesInAs
api.statement: Boundary values: `F(· + iy) → F*` in `L²(ℝ)` as `y → 0`, `‖F*‖_{L²} = ‖F‖`, `y ↦ ‖F(· + iy)‖_{L²}` is nonincreasing, `F → F*` nontangentially almost everywhere, and `F = P[F*]` (mauth2022 Lemma 1 line 359–369, for `H^p(ℂ₊)` with `1 < p < ∞`; garnett2007, Ch. II p. 55, uncertified).

api.name: paleyWienerTheBoundary
api.statement: Paley–Wiener: the boundary map is an isometry of `H²(ℂ₊)` onto `{g ∈ L²(ℝ) : 𝓕g = 0 almost everywhere on (−∞, 0)}` (Mathlib's `𝓕`), and `F(z) = ∫₀^∞ φ(s) e^{isz} ds` with `φ ∈ L²(0, ∞)`, `‖F‖² = 2π‖φ‖²` (mauth2022 Lemma 9 line 469; garnett2007 p. 84, uncertified); in particular `H²(ℂ₊)` is a Hilbert space.

api.name: cauchyFormulaAndFor
api.statement: Cauchy formula: `F(z) = (1/(2πi)) ∫ F*(x)/(x − z) dx` and `∫ F*(x)/(x − conj z) dx = 0` for `z ∈ ℂ₊`; hence `|F(z)|² ≤ ‖F‖²/(4π Im z)` (mauth2022 Lemma 2 line 370–377 states a weaker constant).

api.name: productsForBoundedMultipliers
api.statement: Products: `∫ F*(x) G*(x) dx = 0` for `F, G ∈ H²(ℂ₊)`; bounded multipliers: `GF ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` with `‖GF‖ ≤ sup|G| ‖F‖` for bounded holomorphic `G`.

api.name: logarithmicBound
api.statement: Logarithmic bound: if `F ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` and `F ≢ 0`, then `log|F*| ∈ L¹(Π)`, so `F* ≠ 0` almost everywhere, and `log|F(z)| ≤ P[log|F*|](z)` for every `z ∈ ℂ₊` (garnett2007, Ch. II §4, uncertified). Route: for `ε > 0` the translate `F(· + iε)` is holomorphic near the closed half-plane and bounded there by `‖F‖/√(4πε)` (the point bound above). So §2.5 gives the bound for it, with boundary function `F(· + iε)` on `ℝ`. As `ε → 0`, `log⁺|F(· + iε)| → log⁺|F*|` in `L¹(P(z, x) dx)`. This is because `|log⁺a − log⁺b| ≤ |a − b|` for `a, b ≥ 0`, `F(· + iε) → F*` in `L²(ℝ)`, and `∫ P(z, x)² dx = 1/(2π Im z)`. Take a sequence `εₙ → 0` along which `F(· + iεₙ) → F*` almost everywhere. Fatou's lemma for `log⁻|F(· + iεₙ)|` then gives the bound in the limit at every `z` with `F(z) ≠ 0`. At one such `z` it also gives the integrability of `log⁻|F*|`, while `log⁺|F*| ≤ |F*|²` is integrable.

api.name: weakConvergenceInImplies
api.statement: Weak convergence `Fₙ ⇀ F` in `H²(ℂ₊)` implies locally uniform convergence on `ℂ₊` (mauth2022 Lemma 11 line 487), and `‖M_∞ F‖_{L²} ≤ C‖F‖` (mauth2022 Lemma 6, via §2.3).

api.name: isDefinedByReflection
api.statement: `H²(ℂ₋)` is defined by reflection, and its boundary values are the complex conjugates of those of `H²(ℂ₊)`, orthogonal to them in `L²(ℝ)`.

tests.name: andThePointBound
tests.statement: `F(z) = 1/(z + i)`: `F(z) = −i∫₀^∞ e^{−s} e^{isz} ds`, `‖F‖² = π`, and the point bound at `z = i` is attained: `|F(i)|² = 1/4 = π/(4π)`.

tests.name: theProductOfWith
tests.statement: `∫ dx/(x + i)² = 0`: the product of `1/(z + i)` with itself, as the product law requires.

tests.name: logarithmicBoundEqualityAndStrictCases
tests.statement: Logarithmic bound, equality and strict cases: for `F = 1/(z + i)`, `log|F*| = −log|x + i|` and `P[log|F*|](z) = −log|z + i| = log|F(z)|` (the outer case of §2.8; at `z = i` both sides are `−log 2 ≈ −0.693`). For `F = e^{iz}/(z + i)` the boundary modulus is the same, but `log|F(z)|` is smaller by `Im z`: at `z = i` it is `−1 − log 2 ≈ −1.693 < −0.693`. For `F ≡ 0` the boundary function `log|F*|` is identically `−∞`, so `F ≢ 0` is needed.

tests.name: isNotInThe
tests.statement: `F ≡ 1` is not in `H²(ℂ₊)` (the integrals are infinite), and `1/(z − i)` is not holomorphic on `ℂ₊`.

tests.name: mathlibConventionWitnessFor
tests.statement: Mathlib-convention witness: for `g(x) = 1/(x + i)`, closing the contour in the lower half-plane gives `𝓕g(w) = −2πi e^{−2πw}` for `w > 0`, and `𝓕g(w) = 0` for `w < 0`; the vanishing condition is on the negative frequencies, and a statement with `(0, ∞)` describes `H²(ℂ₋)`.

targets.name: paleyWiener
targets.statement: For `t ≥ 0` define `PW_t` as the set of `F : ℂ → ℂ` with `F(z) = ∫_{−t}^{t} φ(s) e^{isz} ds` for some `φ ∈ L²(−t, t)` (poltoratski2024 line 236–244; mauth2022 Lemma 10 line 472–484). Its API:

api.name: isEntireIsA
api.statement: `F` is entire, `|F(z)| ≤ √(2t) ‖φ‖ e^{t|Im z|}`, `‖F‖²_{L²(ℝ)} = 2π‖φ‖²`, `PW_t` is a closed subspace of `L²(ℝ)`, `PW_s ⊆ PW_t` for `s ≤ t`, and `F ∈ PW_t` implies `F# ∈ PW_t`.

api.name: andConverselyAnEntire
api.statement: `e^{itz}F ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` and `e^{−itz}F ∈ H²(ℂ₋)`; conversely an entire `H` with `e^{itz}H ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` and `e^{−itz}H ∈ H²(ℂ₋)` belongs to `PW_t` (mauth2022 Lemma 10).

api.name: paleyWienerTheoremAn
api.statement: Paley–Wiener theorem: an entire `F` of exponential type at most `t` (`|F(z)| ≤ C_ε e^{(t+ε)|z|}` for every `ε > 0`) whose restriction to `ℝ` is square-integrable belongs to `PW_t`.

api.name: reproducingKernelWithAnd
api.statement: Reproducing kernel: `F(λ) = ∫ F(x) conj(k_t(λ, x)) dx` with `k_t(λ, z) = sin(t(z − conj λ))/(π(z − conj λ))`, and `‖k_t(λ, ·)‖² = k_t(λ, λ) = sinh(2t Im λ)/(2π Im λ)`, equal to `t/π` for real `λ` (poltoratski2024 (2.3)–(2.4) line 241–249).

api.name: exactlyWhenIsAbsolutely
api.statement: `zF ∈ PW_t` exactly when `φ` is absolutely continuous on `[−t, t]` with `φ′ ∈ L²` and `φ(±t) = 0` (then `zF(z) = i∫ φ′(s) e^{isz} ds`); these `F` are dense in `PW_t`.

tests.name: and
tests.statement: `φ = 1_{[−t,t]}`: `F(z) = 2 sin(tz)/z`, and `‖F‖² = ∫ 4 sin²(tx)/x² dx = 4πt = 2π · 2t`.

tests.name: isEntireOfExponential
tests.statement: `e^{itz}` is entire of exponential type `t` but not square-integrable on `ℝ`, and `sin(tz)/z` lies in `PW_t` but not in `PW_s` for `s < t`.

tests.name: kernelNormNumericallyFor
tests.statement: Kernel norm: `∫ sin²(t(y − x))/(π²(y − x)²) dy = t/π` (numerically `0.63657` for `t = 2` against `2/π ≈ 0.63662`).

targets.name: outerFunction
targets.statement: For real `h ∈ L¹(Π)` define the outer function `O_h = exp(S[h])`, and for real `h ∈ L¹(ℝ)` the outer function normalised at infinity `O⁰_h = exp(S⁰[h])`. A holomorphic `F` on `ℂ₊` is outer when `F = c O_h` with `|c| = 1` and `h ∈ L¹(Π)`; `h` is its boundary log-modulus (mauth2022 line 454–468; garnett2007, Ch. II §4, p. 64, uncertified). Its API:
hypotheses: h real, h ∈ L¹(Π) (resp. L¹(ℝ) for the normalisation at infinity)

locator.where: line 454–468, Lemma 8; garnett2007 Ch. II §4 p. 64 (uncertified)

api.name: isHolomorphicAndZero
api.statement: `O_h` is holomorphic and zero-free on `ℂ₊` with `|O_h| = exp P[h]`; by §2.4 its nontangential boundary modulus is `e^{h(x)}` for almost every `x` (mauth2022 Lemma 8 line 463).

api.name: isBoundedExactlyWhen
api.statement: `O_h` is bounded exactly when `h` is essentially bounded above, with `sup |O_h| = e^{ess sup h}`.

api.name: aZeroFreeHolomorphic
api.statement: A zero-free holomorphic `F` on `ℂ₊` with `log|F| = P[h]` is `c O_h` with `|c| = 1`; two outer functions with the same boundary modulus differ by a unimodular constant.

api.name: forEvenIsReal
api.statement: For even `h`, `O_h` is real and positive on the imaginary axis.

api.name: outerMultipliers
api.statement: Outer multipliers: let `F ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` and let `G = c O_h` be outer with `|F*| e^h ∈ L²(ℝ)`. Then `FG ∈ H²(ℂ₊)`, `|(FG)*| = |F*| e^h` almost everywhere, and `‖FG‖ = ‖F* e^h‖_{L²}` (garnett2007, Ch. II §4, uncertified; poltoratski2024 line 685–687 and line 766 and mauth2022 line 945 and line 1137 use it without proof). Route: the case `F ≡ 0` is trivial. Otherwise the logarithmic bound of §2.6 and `log|G| = P[h]` give `2 log|FG(z)| ≤ P[k](z)` with `k = 2 log|F*| + 2h ∈ L¹(Π)`. Jensen's inequality for the probability measure `P(z, x) dx` and the convex function `exp` gives `|FG(z)|² ≤ P[|F*|² e^{2h}](z)`. Integrating in `x` at height `y`, with `∫ P(x + iy, u) dx = 1` and Tonelli, gives `∫ |FG(x + iy)|² dx ≤ ‖F* e^h‖²`. The boundary modulus follows from the nontangential limits of `F` (§2.6) and of `|G| = e^{P[h]}` (§2.4), and the norm identity from `‖FG‖ = ‖(FG)*‖_{L²}` (§2.6).

api.name: boundaryValuesOfOuterFunctions
api.statement: Boundary values of outer functions: if the measure `e^{2h} dx` is Poisson-finite (`∫ e^{2h} dΠ < ∞`), then `O_h/(z + i) ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` by the previous bullet with `F = 1/(z + i)`. So `O_h` has a nontangential limit at almost every `x ∈ ℝ` (§2.6), of modulus `e^{h(x)}`.

tests.name: soAndIsEven
tests.statement: `h(x) = log|x + i|`: `(1/π)∫ log(1 + x²)/(1 + x²) dx = 2 log 2`, so `O_h(i) = 2` and `O_h(z) = −i(z + i)`; `h` is even and `O_h(iy) = y + 1 > 0`.

tests.name: hasBoundaryModulusBut
tests.statement: `e^{iz}` has boundary modulus `1` but is not `c O_0 = c`, and `(z − i)/(z + i)` has a zero; neither is outer.

tests.name: item2
tests.statement: `h = 0`: `O_0 = 1`, and the outer-multiplier bullet reduces to `FG = cF` with `‖FG‖ = ‖F‖`.

tests.name: outerMultiplierComputation
tests.statement: Outer multipliers: for `F = 1/(z + i)²` and `h = log|x + i|` (`G = −i(z + i)`), `FG = −i/(z + i) ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` with `‖FG‖² = π`, and `‖F* e^h‖² = ∫ |x + i|²/|x + i|⁴ dx = ∫ dx/(1 + x²) = π`.

tests.name: boundaryConditionIsNeeded
tests.statement: The boundary condition is needed: `F = 1/(z + i)` with the same `G` has `|F*| e^h = |x + i|/|x + i| = 1`, not in `L²(ℝ)`, and indeed `FG = −i` is not in `H²(ℂ₊)`.

tests.name: outernessIsNeeded
tests.statement: Outerness is needed: `G = e^{−iz}` is zero-free with `|G| = 1` on `ℝ`, but `log|G(z)| = Im z > 0 = P[0](z)`, so it is not outer. For `F = 1/(z + i)`, `|F*| · 1 ∈ L²(ℝ)`, while `FG = e^{−iz}/(z + i)` has `∫ |FG(x + iy)|² dx = πe^{2y}/(y + 1)`, unbounded in `y`.

layers.title: Dirac systems and their Hermite–Biehler functions

targets.name: diracFundamentalMatrix
targets.statement: Define `Q_q(t) = [[g(t), f(t)], [f(t), −g(t)]]` and the fundamental matrix `M_q(t, z)`, `t ≥ 0`, `z ∈ ℂ`, as the propagator `N(t, 0)` (§1.3) on `E = EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 2)` of the coefficient `−Ω(z − Q_q(t))`, acting through `Matrix.toEuclideanCLM`. The coefficient is entire in `z`, with Euclidean operator norm `‖−Ω(z − Q_q(t))‖ ≤ ‖Ω‖(|z| + ‖Q_q(t)‖) = |z| + |q(t)|` (§1.6, Conventions). `M` is the matrix of `N(t, 0)` in the standard basis. Write `M = [[A, B], [C, D]]`, `Θ = (A, C)ᵀ`, `Φ = (B, D)ᵀ` (poltoratski2024 line 136–166; mauth2022 (5)–(6) line 546–563).

api.name: andIsEntireJointly
api.statement: `ΩM(t, z) = Ω + ∫₀ᵗ (z − Q_q(s)) M(s, z) ds`, `M(0, z) = 1`, and `M(t, ·)` is entire, jointly continuous in `(t, z)`.

api.name: theCoefficientIsTrace
api.statement: `det M(t, z) = 1` (§1.4, the coefficient is trace-free; poltoratski2024 (2.1) line 204; mauth2022 Lemma 14 line 565).

api.name: areRealEntireFor
api.statement: `M(t, conj z) = conj M(t, z)`: `A, B, C, D` are real entire, for every complex potential, because `Q_q` has real entries.

api.name: chainRuleForRomanov
api.statement: Chain rule: `M_q(t, z) = M_{q(s+·)}(t − s, z) M_q(s, z)` for `0 ≤ s ≤ t` (romanov2014 line 223–224), and locality: `M_q(t, ·)` depends only on `q` almost everywhere on `[0, t]`.

api.name: inParticularEveryEntry
api.statement: In the Euclidean operator norm, `‖M(t, z)‖ ≤ exp(t|z| + ∫₀ᵗ |q|)`, with equality for a constant potential at `z = 0`; in particular every entry is entire of order at most one and of exponential type at most `t`.

api.name: christoffelDarbouxIdentityRomanov
api.statement: Christoffel–Darboux identity: `M(t, λ)* Ω M(t, z) − Ω = (z − conj λ) ∫₀ᵗ M(s, λ)* M(s, z) ds` (romanov2014 (12) line 758).

api.name: forARealPotential
api.statement: For a real potential, `A(t, −z) = A(t, z)`, `D(t, −z) = D(t, z)`, `B(t, −z) = −B(t, z)`, `C(t, −z) = −C(t, z)`, and `M(t, 0) = diag(e^{F(t)}, e^{−F(t)})` with `F(t) = ∫₀ᵗ f`.

tests.name: freeCase
tests.statement: Free case `q = 0`: `M(t, z) = [[cos tz, −sin tz], [sin tz, cos tz]]`, `det = 1`.

tests.name: realConstantAtThe
tests.statement: Real constant `f = c` at `z = 0`: `M = diag(e^{ct}, e^{−ct})`; the opposite sign convention `ΩX′ = zX + QX` gives `diag(e^{−ct}, e^{ct})`.

tests.name: purelyImaginaryConstantAt
tests.statement: Purely imaginary constant `q = ic` at `z = 0`: `Θ = (cosh ct, −sinh ct)`, `Φ = (−sinh ct, cosh ct)`, `det = cosh² − sinh² = 1`.

tests.name: aSmoothComplexPotential
tests.statement: A smooth complex potential (`f(t) = 0.8 cos 3t + 0.3`, `g(t) = 0.5 sin 2t`, `t = 1.7`, `z = 0.6 + 0.25i`) gives `det M = 1` to twelve digits under numerical integration.

tests.name: normConventionEuclidean
tests.statement: Norm convention: for `q = 1 + i` on `[0, 1]` at `z = 0`, `M(1, 0) = exp(ΩQ_q) = cosh(√2) · 1 + (sinh(√2)/√2) ΩQ_q ≈ [[3.5465, −1.3683], [−1.3683, 0.8099]]`. Its Euclidean operator norm is `e^{√2} ≈ 4.1133`, so the bound `exp(t|z| + ∫|q|)` is attained. Its maximum-row-sum norm is `≈ 4.9148`, so the bound fails for the sup-norm carrier `Fin 2 → ℂ`.

targets.name: diracE
targets.statement: Define `E(t, z) = A(t, z) − iC(t, z)` and `Ẽ(t, z) = B(t, z) − iD(t, z)` (poltoratski2024 line 186–190; mauth2022 line 182–183).

api.name: poltoratskiLineMauthCorollary
api.statement: `det [[E, Ẽ], [E#, Ẽ#]] = E Ẽ# − Ẽ E# = 2i` (poltoratski2024 (2.2) line 205–208; mauth2022 Corollary 2 line 596).

api.name: andAndTheSame
api.statement: `E(0, ·) = 1`, `Ẽ(0, ·) = −i`, and `E(t, z) = 1 + ∫₀ᵗ (−izE(s, z) + q(s)E#(s, z)) ds`, and the same for `Ẽ` (poltoratski2024 (2.5) line 293; mauth2022 Lemma 15 line 612).

api.name: onPoltoratskiLine
api.statement: On `ℝ`: `e^{−∫₀ᵗ|q|} ≤ |E(t, x)|, |Ẽ(t, x)| ≤ e^{∫₀ᵗ|q|}` (poltoratski2024 line 273–275).

api.name: modulusAndArgumentWith
api.statement: Modulus and argument: with the continuous branch `φ(t, x)` of `arg E(t, x)` in `(t, x)` normalised by `φ(0, x) = 0`, `∂ₜ log|E| = f cos 2φ + g sin 2φ` and `∂ₜ φ = −x + g cos 2φ − f sin 2φ` almost everywhere; for real potentials these are poltoratski2024 (2.6)–(2.7) (line 295–306) and mauth2022 Lemma 17 (line 646), and `φ(t, 0) = 0`.

api.name: kernelIdentity
api.statement: Kernel identity: `(A(t, z) conj C(t, w) − C(t, z) conj A(t, w))/(conj w − z) = ∫₀ᵗ Θ(s, w)* Θ(s, z) ds`.

tests.name: freeCaseAnd
tests.statement: Free case: `E = e^{−itz}`, `Ẽ = −i e^{−itz}`, and `E Ẽ# − Ẽ E# = e^{−itz}(i e^{itz}) + i e^{−itz}e^{itz} = 2i`.

tests.name: realConstantAtAnd
tests.statement: Real constant `f = c` at `z = 0`: `E(t, 0) = e^{ct}`, `Ẽ(t, 0) = −i e^{−ct}`, and the upper bound `e^{∫|q|} = e^{ct}` is attained, so the bound is sharp.

tests.name: theReflectionIsNeeded
tests.statement: The reflection is needed in the equation: `∂ₜE = −izE + qE` (without `#`) would give `E(t, 0) = e^{ict}` for `q = ic`, while the solution of §3.1 gives `cosh ct + i sinh ct`.

targets.name: IsHermiteBiehler
targets.statement: Call an entire `H` Hermite–Biehler when `|H#(z)| < |H(z)|` for every `z ∈ ℂ₊` (poltoratski2024 line 175–180; mauth2022 line 491–493). Its API:

locator.where: line 175–180; mauth2022 Lemma 13 line 531; romanov2014 Proposition 4 line 780

api.name: aHermiteBiehlerFunction
api.statement: A Hermite–Biehler function has no zeros in `ℂ₊`, and `H#/H` is bounded by `1` on `ℂ₊`.

api.name: forAndAreHermite
api.statement: For `t > 0`, `E(t, ·)` and `Ẽ(t, ·)` are Hermite–Biehler, with `|E(t, z)|² − |E#(t, z)|² = 4 Im z ∫₀ᵗ |Θ(s, z)|² ds` and `|Ẽ(t, z)|² − |Ẽ#(t, z)|² = 4 Im z ∫₀ᵗ |Φ(s, z)|² ds` (mauth2022 Lemma 13 line 531; romanov2014 Proposition 4 line 780, identity (15)).

api.name: andHaveNoZeros
api.statement: `E(t, ·)` and `Ẽ(t, ·)` have no zeros in the closed upper half-plane (on `ℝ` by §3.2), and are entire of order at most one and exponential type at most `t` (§3.1).

api.name: routeTheChristoffelDarboux
api.statement: Route: the Christoffel–Darboux identity at `λ = z` and `|u − iv|² − |u + iv|² = 4 Im(conj(u) v)`.

tests.name: freeCaseAnd
tests.statement: Free case: `|E|² − |E#|² = e^{2ty} − e^{−2ty} = 2 sinh 2ty`, and `4y ∫₀ᵗ (|cos sz|² + |sin sz|²) ds = 4y ∫₀ᵗ cosh 2sy ds = 2 sinh 2ty`.

tests.name: hasSoIsNeeded
tests.statement: `t = 0`: `E = 1` has `|E#| = |E|`, so `t > 0` is needed.

tests.name: isNotHermiteBiehler
tests.statement: `H(z) = z − i` is not Hermite–Biehler (`|z + i| > |z − i|` on `ℂ₊`), while `z + i` is.

tests.name: theSmoothComplexPotential
tests.statement: The smooth complex potential of §3.1 gives `|E(t, z)| ≈ 1.841 > 0.573 ≈ |E#(t, z)|`.

layers.title: Scattering data on a finite interval

targets.name: scatteringMatrix
targets.statement: Define the scattering matrix `G_q(t, z)` as the propagator `N(t, 0)` (§1.3) on `EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 2)` of the coefficient `[[0, e^{−2izt} conj q(t)], [e^{2izt} q(t), 0]]`, entire in `z` with operator norm `max(|e^{−2izt}|, |e^{2izt}|) |q(t)| = |q(t)| e^{2t|Im z|}` (§1.6), and the scattering functions `a = (G_q)₂₂`, `b = (G_q)₂₁` (poltoratski2024 (5.3) line 492–501).

api.name: structureAndOnSo
api.statement: Structure: `G_q = [[a#, b#], [b, a]]` and `det G_q = a a# − b b# = 1`; on `ℝ`, `|a(t, x)|² − |b(t, x)|² = 1`, so `G_q(t, x) ∈ SU(1,1)` (poltoratski2024 line 501–503).

api.name: dictionaryWithEquivalentlyAnd
api.statement: Dictionary with §3.2: `a = e^{itz}(E + iẼ)/2`, `b = e^{itz}(E − iẼ)/2`, equivalently `E = e^{−itz}(a + b)` and `Ẽ = −i e^{−itz}(a − b)` (poltoratski2024 (5.2) line 484–488; mauth2022 line 187–189).

api.name: volterraFormAndPoltoratski
api.statement: Volterra form: `a(t, z) = 1 + ∫₀ᵗ q(s) e^{2izs} b#(s, z) ds` and `b(t, z) = ∫₀ᵗ q(s) e^{2izs} a#(s, z) ds` (poltoratski2024 (5.4) line 508–517).

api.name: localityDependsOnlyOn
api.statement: Locality: `G_q(t, ·)` depends only on `q` almost everywhere on `[0, t]`; if `q = 0` on `(T, t)` then `G_q(t, ·) = G_q(T, ·)`.

api.name: concatenationForWithAnd
api.statement: Concatenation: for `0 ≤ s ≤ t`, with `(a₁, b₁) = (a_q(s, ·), b_q(s, ·))` and `(a₂, b₂)` the scattering functions of `q(s + ·)` at time `t − s`, `b_q(t) = e^{2izs} b₂ a₁# + a₂ b₁` and `a_q(t) = e^{2izs} b₂ b₁# + a₂ a₁`.

api.name: translationOfThePotential
api.statement: Translation of the potential: for `t₀ ≥ 0` and `q^{t₀}(s) = q(s − t₀) 1_{s ≥ t₀}`, `a_{q^{t₀}}(t + t₀, z) = a_q(t, z)` and `b_{q^{t₀}}(t + t₀, z) = e^{2izt₀} b_q(t, z)`.

api.name: modulationOfThePotential
api.statement: Modulation of the potential: for `ξ ∈ ℝ`, `G_{q e^{2iξ·}}(t, z) = G_q(t, z + ξ)`.

api.name: dilationFor
api.statement: Dilation: for `λ > 0`, `G_{λ q(λ·)}(t, z) = G_q(λt, z/λ)`.

api.name: realPotentialsAndAnd
api.statement: Real potentials: `a(t, −conj z) = conj a(t, z)` and `b(t, −conj z) = conj b(t, z)`; `a(t, iy)` and `b(t, iy)` are real, and `a(t, 0) = cosh F(t)`, `b(t, 0) = sinh F(t)` with `F(t) = ∫₀ᵗ f`.

tests.name: freeCase
tests.statement: Free case: `G = 1`, `a = 1`, `b = 0`.

tests.name: positionOfForThe
tests.statement: Position of `q`: for the smooth complex potential of §3.1 the dictionary values `a ≈ 1.0632 + 0.1443i`, `b ≈ 0.0750 + 0.2463i` agree with the solution of the defining system to twelve digits, while the system with `conj q` in the lower left entry gives `a ≈ 1.2589 − 0.1142i`, `b ≈ 0.6221 − 0.2396i`; the first-order term of `b` is `∫ q e^{2izs}`, not `∫ conj q e^{2izs}`.

tests.name: taoThieleConventionFor
tests.statement: Tao–Thiele convention: for `q = 1` on `[0, 1]`, `|a(1, 5i)| ≈ 1.093 ≤ cosh 1`, while `|a(1, −5i)| ≈ 237.0`; the function bounded on `ℂ₊` is the present `a`, whose reflection is Tao and Thiele's `a`.

tests.name: translationForOnThe
tests.statement: Translation: for `q(s) = 0.4 cos 5s + 0.3i` on `[0, 1]`, `t₀ = 0.6`, `z = 0.3 + 0.1i`, the translated potential gives `a` equal to `a_q(1, z)` and `b` equal to `e^{2izt₀} b_q(1, z)` up to the discretisation error.

targets.name: norm_scatteringA_le_cosh
targets.statement: Let `L = ∫₀ᵗ |q|`. Prove that for `z` in the closed upper half-plane `|a(t, z)| ≤ cosh L`, `|a(t, z) − 1| ≤ cosh L − 1`, `|b(t, z)| ≤ sinh L` and `|b(t, z) − ∫₀ᵗ q(s) e^{2izs} ds| ≤ sinh L − L`; that `a(t, z) → 1` and `b(t, z) → 0` as `|z| → ∞` in the closed half-plane; and that for `q` integrable on `[0, ∞)` the functions `a(t, ·)`, `b(t, ·)` converge uniformly on the closed half-plane as `t → ∞`. Route: the `n`-th Dyson term of `a` or `b` is an integral over the simplex `s₁ < ⋯ < sₙ < t` of `q(sₙ) conj q(sₙ₋₁) ⋯` times `e^{2izσ}` with an alternating sum `σ ≥ 0`, so it is bounded by `Lⁿ/n!`; decay is the Riemann–Lebesgue lemma for the image of the simplex integrand under `σ`, uniform over the compact family `e^{−2σ Im z}`. For the discrete analogue on `ℓ¹`, see taothiele2012 Lecture 1 §3: Lemma 5 (line 430–433) gives the uniform convergence of truncations, and line 460–465 gives the bound `sup arccosh|a| ≤ Σ arccosh((1 − |F_n|²)^{−1/2})` on the circle.
hypotheses: q integrable on [0,t] (on [0,∞) for the uniform limit)

locator.where: Lecture 1 §3 Lemma 5 line 430–433 and line 460–465 (discrete analogue on ℓ¹)

tests.name: onTheOpenLower
tests.statement: On the open lower half-plane no bound holds: `|a(1, −5i)| ≈ 237`.

targets.name: one_le_normSq_scatteringA_sub_normSq_scatteringB
targets.statement: Prove that `|a(t, z)|² − |b(t, z)|² ≥ 1` for every `z` in the closed upper half-plane, with equality on `ℝ`; hence `|a(t, z)| ≥ 1`, `|b(t, z)| < |a(t, z)|`, `a(t, ·)` has no zeros in the closed half-plane, and `ρ(t, ·) = b(t, ·)/a(t, ·)` is holomorphic on a neighbourhood of the closed half-plane with `1 − |ρ(t, z)|² ≥ 1/|a(t, z)|²` (poltoratski2024 line 503–507; taothiele2012 Lemma 3 line 296 for the discrete model). Route: for `X = M(·, z)c`, `h(X) = Im(conj u · v)` satisfies `∂ₜh = Im z |X|² ≥ 2 Im z h` and `|u − iv|² − |u + iv|² = 4h`. For `c = c₁(1, i) + c₂(1, −i)` one has `h(c) = |c₁|² − |c₂|²`, `u − iv = 2e^{−itz}(c₁a + c₂b)` and `u + iv = 2e^{itz}(c₁b# + c₂a#)`, so `|c₁ a + c₂ b|² ≥ |c₁|² − |c₂|²` whenever `|c₂| ≤ |c₁|`; minimising over `c₂` gives `|a|² ≥ 1 + |b|²`.

tests.name: constantPotentialsOnAnd
tests.statement: Constant potentials `q ∈ {1, 0.3 + 2i, 3}` on `[0, 1]` and `z` on a grid of the closed half-plane give `min(|a|² − |b|²) = 1.0000` (attained on `ℝ`) and `min |a| ≈ 1.006`.

tests.name: realAt
tests.statement: Real `f` at `z = 0`: `|a|² − |b|² = cosh² F − sinh² F = 1`.

tests.name: theInequalityFailsIn
tests.statement: The inequality fails in the lower half-plane: `q = 1` on `[0, 1]` at `z = −5i` gives `|a| ≈ 237 < |b| ≈ 2385`.

targets.name: integral_log_norm_scatteringA
targets.statement: Let `q` be square-integrable on `[0, t]`. Prove that `log a(t, ·)` (the logarithm vanishing at `i∞`) is a bounded holomorphic function on `ℂ₊`, that `y(a(t, iy) − 1) → ½∫₀ᵗ |q|²` as `y → ∞`, and the non-linear Plancherel identity `∫_ℝ log|a(t, x)| dx = (π/2) ∫₀ᵗ |q|²`; hence `log|a(t, ·)| ∈ L¹(ℝ)`, `a(t, ·) = O⁰_{log|a(t,·)|}` is outer, `log(1 − |ρ(t, x)|²) = −2 log|a(t, x)|` on `ℝ`, and `∫ −log(1 − |ρ(t, x)|²) dx = π ∫₀ᵗ |q|²`. For real potentials `a(t, iy) > 0` (poltoratski2024 (5.5) line 545–548 and line 503–507, printed with constant `1`; denisov2006 (194) line 3250–3255; taothiele2012 Lemma 6 line 680–683 for the discrete model). Route: `log a(t, ·)` is a primitive of `∂_z a/a` on `ℂ₊` (Tau Ceti `DifferentiableOn.hasDerivAt_wedgeIntegral_upperHalfPlane`), bounded and continuous to `ℝ` by §4.2–§4.3; §2.5 gives `log|a(t, z)| = P[log|a(t, ·)|](z)`; §2.2 gives `πy log|a(t, iy)| ↑ ∫ log|a(t, x)| dx`; the Volterra form with the approximate identity `y e^{−2yu} 1_{u>0}` (mass `1/2`) gives the limit at `i∞`.

locator.where: (5.5) line 545–548 (printed with constant 1); denisov2006 (194) line 3250–3255; taothiele2012 Lemma 6 line 680–683

tests.name: firstOrderForSmall
tests.statement: First order: for small `q`, `log|a| ≈ ½|b|²` and `∫ |∫₀ᵗ q e^{2ixs} ds|² dx = π∫₀ᵗ|q|²`, giving `π/2` again; the constant `1` printed in the sources fails this computation.

targets.name: scatteringA_eq_exp_integral_riccati
targets.statement: For `z` in the closed upper half-plane define `r(t, z) = e^{2izt} b#(t, z)/a(t, z)`. Prove that `|r(t, z)| < 1`, that `∂ₜ r = 2iz r + conj q − q r²` with `r(0, z) = 0`, that `a(t, z) = exp(∫₀ᵗ q(s) r(s, z) ds)`, that `|r(t, z)| ≤ 2∫₀ᵗ e^{−2 Im z (t − s)} |q(s)| ds`, and that `ρ(t, z) = ∫₀ᵗ q(s) e^{2izs} a(s, z)^{−2} ds`. Route: with `β = e^{2izt} b#`, the pair `(a, β)` solves `a′ = qβ`, `β′ = 2izβ + conj q a`, so `∂ₜ(|a|² − |β|²) = 4 Im z |β|² ≥ 0`, and `r = β/a` satisfies the Riccati equation; `∂ₜ ρ = q e^{2izt}/a²` follows from `det G = 1`. For the Krein-system analogue, the Riccati equation of the Schur function of the system restricted to a tail `[s, ∞)`, see denisov2006 §9 Lemma 9.1 (157)–(158) line 2510–2521, and Lemma 9.2 line 2544–2556 for its solution as the ratio of the two components of a linear system.

tests.name: freeCase
tests.statement: Free case: `r = 0`, `a = 1`, `ρ = 0`.

tests.name: forTheSmoothComplex

Its API:

Prove that `B(E(t, ·)) = PW_t` and `B(Ẽ(t, ·)) = PW_t` as sets, with `e^{−∫₀ᵗ|q|} ‖F‖_{L²} ≤ ‖F‖_{B(E(t,·))} ≤ e^{∫₀ᵗ|q|} ‖F‖_{L²}`, and that the reproducing kernels are `K_t(w, z) = (1/π) ∫₀ᵗ Θ(s, w)* Θ(s, z) ds` and `K̃_t(w, z) = (1/π) ∫₀ᵗ Φ(s, w)* Φ(s, z) ds` (poltoratski2024 line 269–285; mauth2022 Lemma 18 line 659–691; romanov2014 Theorem 5 (16) line 812). targets.name: norm_deBrangesSpace_diracE_eq
targets.statement: Prove that for `0 < s ≤ t` and `F ∈ PW_s`, `‖F‖_{B(E(t,·))} = ‖F‖_{B(E(s,·))}`, and the same for `Ẽ` (poltoratski2024 line 255–262; romanov2014 §8 Theorem 16 line 2283 by an operator-theoretic route). Route: fix `x ∈ ℝ`. The map `r ↦ E(r, x)` is absolutely continuous on `[s, t]` (§1.2, applied to `Θ(·, x)` and followed by the linear map `(u, v) ↦ u − iv`), and `|E(r, x)| ≥ c = e^{−∫₀ᵗ|q|}` there (§3.2). So `r ↦ |E(r, x)|^{−2}`, which is `E(·, x)` followed by the Lipschitz map `w ↦ max(|w|, c)^{−2}`, is absolutely continuous on `[s, t]` (Mathlib `LipschitzWith.comp_absolutelyContinuousOnInterval`), with derivative `−2 Re(q(r)/E(r, x)²)` at almost every `r` (§3.2). Mathlib `AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval.integral_deriv_eq_sub` gives, for every `x`, `|E(t, x)|^{−2} − |E(s, x)|^{−2} = −2∫_s^t Re(q(r)/E(r, x)²) dr`. Multiply by `|F(x)|² = F(x)F#(x)` and integrate over `ℝ`. The integrand is bounded by `2|F(x)|²|q(r)| e^{2∫₀ʳ|q|}`, which is integrable on `[s, t] × ℝ`, so the two integrals may be exchanged (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.intervalIntegral_integral_swap`): `‖F‖²_{B(E(t,·))} − ‖F‖²_{B(E(s,·))} = −2∫_s^t Re(q(r) ∫ (F/E(r, ·))(F#/E(r, ·)) dx) dr`. For every `r ∈ [s, t]`, `F ∈ PW_s ⊆ PW_r`, so `F/E(r, ·)` and `F#/E(r, ·)` lie in `H²(ℂ₊)` (§6.2) and the inner integral vanishes by the product law of §2.6. The same argument with `Ẽ`, which satisfies the same equation and the same bounds (§3.2), gives the identity for `Ẽ`.

The integrated identity holds there: `e^{−2t} − e^{−2s} = −2∫_s^t e^{−2r} dr` for `0 ≤ s ≤ t ≤ 1`, and both sides are constant in `t` beyond `1`, where `q = 0`.

Writing `(u, v) = Φ(t, z) + wΘ(t, z)`, its boundary circle consists of the `w` with `u/v ∈ ℝ ∪ {∞}`, among them `−D(t, z)/C(t, z)` and `−B(t, z)/A(t, z)` (`A(t, z)` and `C(t, z)` do not vanish, since `Im(conj A(t, z) · C(t, z)) = Im z ∫₀ᵗ |Θ(s, z)|² ds > 0`), while `−Ẽ(t, z)/E(t, z)`, the point where `u − iv` vanishes, lies in its interior. api.name: weylFunctionOfCompactSupport
api.statement: Compact support: if `q = 0` almost everywhere on `(T, ∞)` for some `T ≥ 0`, then `m = −Ẽ(T, ·)/E(T, ·)` on `ℂ₊`. Beyond `T` the system is free, so `E(t, z) = e^{−i(t−T)z} E(T, z)` and likewise for `Ẽ` (§3.2), and for `t ≥ T` the solution `(u, v) = Φ + wΘ` has `(u − iv)(t) = e^{−i(t−T)z}(Ẽ(T, z) + wE(T, z))`, of modulus growing like `e^{(t−T) Im z}` unless it vanishes, and `(u + iv)(t) = e^{i(t−T)z}(Ẽ#(T, z) + wE#(T, z))`, which decays. As `|u|² + |v|² = (|u − iv|² + |u + iv|²)/2`, `Φ + wΘ` is square-integrable exactly when `Ẽ(T, z) + wE(T, z) = 0`, and `E(T, z) ≠ 0` on `ℂ₊` (§3.3).

api.name: isHolomorphicOnWith
api.statement: `m` is holomorphic on `ℂ₊` with `Im m > 0`, and `−Ẽ(t, ·)/E(t, ·) → m` locally uniformly on `ℂ₊`, with error at most twice the radius.

api.name: theDirichletWeylFunction
api.statement: The Dirichlet Weyl function is `−1/m = lim E(t, ·)/Ẽ(t, ·)`.

api.name: routeOfAtTime
api.statement: Route: `Im(conj u · v)` of `Φ + wΘ` at time `t` is `−Im w + Im z ∫₀ᵗ|Φ + wΘ|²` by the Christoffel–Darboux identity; nesting is monotonicity in `t`; since `A, B, C, D` are real entire (§3.1), `(u − iv)(t) = Ẽ(t, z) + wE(t, z)` and `(u + iv)(t) = Ẽ#(t, z) + wE#(t, z)`, and `Im(conj u · v) = (|u − iv|² − |u + iv|²)/4` gives the second description, a disc because `|E(t, z)| > |E#(t, z)|` (§3.3); `u − iv` vanishes at `w = −Ẽ/E`, where `u + iv ≠ 0` because `(u, v) ≠ 0`, so that point lies inside the disc. Limit point: if `Θ(·, z₀) ∈ L²` for some `z₀ ∈ ℂ₊`, then `Φ(·, z₀) ∈ L²` as well, since `Φ + wΘ` is square-integrable for `w` in the nonempty `⋂_t D_t(z₀)`. So at `λ₀ = −z₀` the square-integrable solutions do not form a line, `∞` is a limit-circle endpoint by the alternative of OperatorTheory/UnboundedOperators §4.8 (dictionary of the Conventions), and every solution is square-integrable at every `z`, in particular at `z = 0`; there `det[Θ, Φ] = 1` gives `1 ≤ |Θ||Φ|`, which is not integrable on `[0, ∞)`.

tests.name: freeCaseForEvery
tests.statement: Free case: `−Ẽ/E = i` for every `t`, `m = i`, and `Φ + iΘ = (i e^{itz}, e^{itz})` is square-integrable on `ℝ₊` for `z ∈ ℂ₊`; the radius is `1/sinh(2t Im z) → 0`. Under the dictionary of the Conventions this is the limit-point case of OperatorTheory/UnboundedOperators §4.8 at `λ = −z ∈ ℂ₋`: the square-integrable solutions are the multiples of `(i e^{itz}, e^{itz})`, while `Φ − iΘ = (−i e^{−itz}, e^{−itz})` grows like `e^{t Im z}`.

tests.name: weylPointIsInterior
tests.statement: `−Ẽ/E` is interior, not a boundary point. Free case, `t = 1.7`, `z = 0.6 + 0.25i`: at `w = −Ẽ/E = i`, `Im z ∫₀ᵗ |Φ + iΘ|² = 1 − e^{−2t Im z} = 1 − e^{−0.85} ≈ 0.5726 < 1 = Im i`; the disc is `|w − i| ≤ e^{−2t Im z} |w + i|`, with centre `i coth(0.85) ≈ 1.4470i` and radius `1/sinh(0.85) ≈ 1.0459`, at distance `0.4470` from `i`, while `−D/C = −cot(tz)`, where `v = 0`, lies on the circle. For the smooth complex potential of §3.1 at the same `t` and `z`, `w₀ = −Ẽ/E ≈ 0.3468 + 0.7493i` has `Im z ∫₀ᵗ |Φ + w₀Θ|² ≈ 0.4541 < Im w₀`, and the disc `|Ẽ + wE| ≤ |Ẽ# + wE#|` has radius `≈ 0.6538`, equal to the stated radius, with `−D/C` and `−B/A` on its circle. A description with `−Ẽ/E` on the boundary would force equality in both instances.

tests.name: onByForThe
tests.statement: On `ℝ`, `Im(−Ẽ(t, x)/E(t, x)) = 1/|E(t, x)|²` by `det M = 1`; for the smooth complex potential of §3.1 at `x = 0.7`, both sides are `0.983136`, and `Im(E/Ẽ) = 1/|Ẽ|² = 0.838119`.

tests.name: compactSupportComputed
tests.statement: Compact support, computed: in the free case the formula gives `−Ẽ(T, ·)/E(T, ·) = i = m` for every `T`. For `f = 1` on `[0, 1]`, zero afterwards, at `z = i` it gives `m(i) = i/(1 + √2 tanh √2) ≈ 0.443190i`; with this `w`, `u − iv` vanishes at `t = 1` and `∫₀^∞ |Φ + wΘ|² = Im m(i)/Im z ≈ 0.443190` (`≈ 0.401791` on `[0, 1]` and `|u + iv|²/4 ≈ 0.041399` on the free tail), while `w = m(i) + 0.01` leaves `|u − iv| ≈ 0.0491` at `t = 1`, so the solution grows like `e^{t−1}`. The boundary points `−D(1, i)/C(1, i) ≈ 0.591892i` and `−B(1, i)/A(1, i) ≈ 0.385819i` of `D_1(i)`, the ends of a diameter of length `≈ 0.206073`, are not `m(i)`.

targets.name: spectralMeasure
targets.statement: Define the Neumann spectral measure `μ_q` as the Poisson-finite measure of §2.2 for the positive harmonic function `Im m`, so that `Im m = β Im z + P[μ_q]` with `β ≥ 0`, and the Dirichlet spectral measure `μ̃_q` likewise for `Im(−1/m)`; write `μ = w dx + μ_s` and `μ̃ = w̃ dx + μ̃_s` (poltoratski2024 line 255–264; mauth2022 line 692–701; romanov2014 line 2275–2281). Equivalently, `(Re m(i), β, μ_q/π)` is the triple of `m` in AutomorphicSpectralTheory §0.5, so `m(z) = Re m(i) + βz + (1/π)∫ ((x − z)⁻¹ − x/(1 + x²)) dμ_q(x)`. Its API:

api.name: andAtAlmostEvery
api.statement: `w(x) = Im m(x + i0)` and `w̃(x) = Im(−1/m)(x + i0) = w(x)/|m(x + i0)|²` at almost every `x` where the nontangential limit `m(x + i0)` exists and is finite and nonzero (§2.4); hence `w w̃ ≤ 1` almost everywhere.

api.name: compactSupportIfOn
api.statement: Compact support: if `q = 0` on `(T, ∞)` then `β = 0`, `μ_q = dx/|E(T, x)|²` and `μ̃_q = dx/|Ẽ(T, x)|²`.

api.name: freeCase
api.statement: Free case: `μ = μ̃ = dx`.

api.name: andAreDeterminedBy
api.statement: `μ_q` and `μ̃_q` are determined by `m`, which depends only on `q` on `[0, ∞)`.

api.name: truncationsConvergeWeakly
api.statement: Truncations: let `C = TauCeti.boundaryCayley`, let `μ_T = dx/|E(T, ·)|²` be the Neumann spectral measure of the truncation `q_T` (compact-support bullet) and `m_T = −Ẽ(T, ·)/E(T, ·)` its Weyl function (§6.4), and on Mathlib's `Circle`, written `X`, let `ν_T = C_*(μ_T/(π(1 + x²)))` and `ν = C_*(μ_q/(π(1 + x²))) + β δ₁`. Then `m(z) = Re m(i) + i H_ν((z − i)/(z + i))` on `ℂ₊`, where `H_ν(ξ) = ∫ (ζ + ξ)/(ζ − ξ) dν(ζ)` is the Herglotz transform, and likewise `m_T(z) = Re m_T(i) + i H_{ν_T}((z − i)/(z + i))`; the masses satisfy `ν_T(X) = Im m_T(i) → Im m(i) = ν(X)`; and `ν_T → ν` weakly on the circle as `T → ∞`. Route: the identity is Tau Ceti `TauCeti.I_mul_herglotzTransform_cayley_eq` for `ν`, whose atom at `1` is `β` and whose Cayley pushforward is `μ_q/(π(1 + x²))`, compared with the representation above through `(1 + xz)/(x − z) = (1 + x²)((x − z)⁻¹ − x/(1 + x²))`; the masses are `H(0)` (Tau Ceti `MeasureTheory.Measure.herglotzTransform_zero`), the value at `z = i`. Since `m_T → m` locally uniformly on `ℂ₊` (§6.4), `H_{ν_T} → H_ν` uniformly on `|ξ| = 1/2`. For `k ≥ 1` the coefficient of `ξᵏ` in `H_ν(ξ)` is `2∫ ζ̄ᵏ dν(ζ)`, so every Fourier coefficient of `ν_T` tends to that of `ν`. The masses are bounded and the trigonometric polynomials are dense in the continuous functions on the circle (Mathlib `span_fourier_closure_eq_top`, carried to `Circle` by `AddCircle.homeomorphCircle'`), so `∫ g dν_T → ∫ g dν` for every continuous `g`, which is weak convergence (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.FiniteMeasure.tendsto_iff_forall_integral_rclike_tendsto`).

tests.name: freeCase
tests.statement: Free case: `m = i`, `Im m ≡ 1 = P[dx]`, `μ = dx`, `β = 0`.

tests.name: realConstantOnZero
tests.statement: Real constant `f = c` on `[0, T]`, zero afterwards, at `x = 0`: `m(0) = −Ẽ(T, 0)/E(T, 0) = i e^{−2cT}`, so `w(0) = e^{−2cT}`, `w̃(0) = e^{2cT}` and `w w̃ = 1` there; the inequality `w w̃ ≤ 1` is strict exactly where `Re m(x + i0) ≠ 0`.

tests.name: aConstantPotentialOn
tests.statement: A constant potential on all of `[0, ∞)`, `f ≡ c > 0`, has `w = 0` on `(−c, c)` (exponentially growing and decaying real solutions), so `μ` is not equivalent to Lebesgue measure without a decay hypothesis.

tests.name: truncationsFreeCase
tests.statement: Truncations, free case: `μ_T = dx` and `ν_T = C_*(dx/(π(1 + x²)))`, normalised arc length, for every `T`; `H_{ν_T} ≡ 1`, so `m_T = i`, and the mass is `1 = Im i`.

tests.name: truncationsMasses
tests.statement: Truncations, masses: for `f ≡ 1` on `[0, ∞)` the Weyl function is `m(z) = (1 + iκ)/z` with `κ = √(z² − 1)`, `Im κ > 0`, so `Im m(i) = √2 − 1 ≈ 0.414214`; the masses `Im m_T(i)` are `0.537329`, `0.443190`, `0.415910`, `0.414219` at `T = 0.5, 1, 2, 4`.

tests.name: truncationsWeakNotPointwise
tests.statement: Truncations, weak and not pointwise: for the same `f ≡ 1` at `x = 2`, the density `1/|E(T, 2)|²` oscillates in `T` between `1/2` and `3/2` with period `π/√3` and has no limit, while the limit density is `w(2) = Im m(2 + i0) = √3/2 ≈ 0.866025`, its mean over a period. Convergence of the densities is not part of the statement and fails.

targets.name: integral_normSq_spectralMeasure_eq
targets.statement: Prove that for every `t > 0` and `F ∈ PW_t`, `∫ |F|² dμ_q = ‖F‖²_{B(E(t,·))}` and `∫ |F|² dμ̃_q = ‖F‖²_{B(Ẽ(t,·))}`, and that `μ_q` is the only Poisson-finite measure with the first property for all `t > 0` (poltoratski2024 line 255–262; romanov2014 §8 Theorem 16 line 2283–2363; debranges1968 §§19–23 and remling2018 Ch. 3, waived). Route: the measures `μ_T = dx/|E(T, ·)|²` of the truncations `q_T` (§6.5) have Cayley images `C_*(μ_T/(π(1 + x²)))` that converge weakly on the circle to `C_*(μ/(π(1 + x²))) + β δ₁` (truncation bullet of §6.5); for `F ∈ PW_t` with `zF ∈ PW_t`, `(1 + x²)|F(x)|² → 0` at `±∞`, so `∫|F|² dμ_T → ∫|F|² dμ`, while `∫|F|² dμ_T = ‖F‖²_{B(E(t,·))}` for `T ≥ t` by §6.3; such `F` are dense in `PW_t` (§2.7), and Cauchy sequences in `B(E(t, ·))` are Cauchy in `L²(μ)`. Uniqueness: two such measures give equal finite measures `|k_ε|² dμ` for `k_ε(x) = sin(εx)/x`, by Mathlib `Measure.ext_of_charFun` applied to `e^{iax}k_ε` and `k_ε`.

tests.statement: Free case: Plancherel `∫ |F|² dx = ‖F‖²_{L²}`.

tests.statement: Compact support `q = q_T`: for `t ≥ T` the identity is the definition of `μ`, and for `t < T` it is §6.3.

tests.statement: `2 dx` fails the identity in the free case (`∫ |F|² 2dx = 2‖F‖²`), so the normalisation of `μ` is forced.

tests.name: timeZeroExcluded
tests.statement: `t = 0`: `E(0, ·) = 1` is not Hermite–Biehler, so `B(E(0, ·))` is not defined (§6.1), and `PW_0 = {0}`; the statement is for `t > 0`, as in §6.2 and §6.3, and loses nothing.

targets.name: klDiv_cayley_poissonMeasure_spectralMeasure
targets.statement: Write `X` for Mathlib's `Circle`, `C = TauCeti.boundaryCayley` for the boundary Cayley map `x ↦ (x − i)/(x + i)`, and `σ = C_*(Π/π)`, which is normalised arc length `dθ/2π`. For a Poisson-finite measure `μ` on `ℝ` with Lebesgue decomposition `μ = w dx + μ_s` (Mathlib `Measure.rnDeriv` and `Measure.singularPart` with respect to Lebesgue measure) and `β ≥ 0`, let `ν_{μ,β} = C_*(μ/(π(1 + x²))) + β δ₁`, a finite measure on `X` of mass `β + (1/π)∫ dμ/(1 + x²)`. The entropy of `σ` relative to `ν` in the sense of killipsimon2003 ((5.9) line 1812–1819, (5.10) line 1831–1834) is, in Mathlib's terms, `S(σ | ν) = ν(X) − σ(X) − klDiv σ ν`, read as `−∞` when `klDiv σ ν = ∞` (Mathlib `InformationTheory.klDiv`). The facts the source proves about it are in the pinned libraries: the bound `S(σ | ν) ≤ log ν(X)` for a probability measure `σ` (killipsimon2003 Lemma 5.1 line 1836) is Mathlib `InformationTheory.mul_log_le_klDiv` at `σ(X) = 1`; the variational formula (Theorem 5.2 line 1864) is Tau Ceti `TauCeti.klDiv_eq_iSup_boundedContinuousFunction_integral_sub_integral_exp_sub_one` with `F = e^f`; and the joint weak upper semicontinuity of `S` (Corollary 5.3 line 1960) is `TauCeti.lowerSemicontinuous_klDiv_finiteMeasure` together with the continuity of the total mass under weak convergence. Prove that `klDiv σ ν_{μ,β} = ν_{μ,β}(X) − 1 − (1/π) ∫ log w dΠ` when `w > 0` almost everywhere and `log w ∈ L¹(Π)`, and that `klDiv σ ν_{μ,β} = ∞` otherwise; equivalently `S(σ | ν_{μ,β}) = (1/π) ∫ log w dΠ` in `[−∞, ∞)`. Route: `log⁺ w ≤ w` and `∫ w dΠ ≤ ∫ dμ/(1 + x²) < ∞`, so the positive part of `log w` is always `Π`-integrable; `σ` has no atoms and is equivalent to arc length, while `C_*(μ_s)` and the atom are singular to arc length, so `σ ≪ ν_{μ,β}` exactly when `w > 0` almost everywhere, and then `dσ/dν_{μ,β}` is `1/w` carried by `C`, `σ`-almost everywhere; changing variables along `C` gives `∫ llr σ ν_{μ,β} dσ = −(1/π) ∫ log w dΠ`, which is finite exactly when `log w ∈ L¹(Π)`.

σ = C_*(Π/π), ν_{μ,β} = C_*(μ/(π(1 + x²))) + β δ₁ on Mathlib's Circle, C = TauCeti.boundaryCayley
first case: w > 0 almost everywhere and log w ∈ L¹(Π)

tests.name: sigmaIsArcLengthAndFreeCase
tests.statement: `σ` is arc length: the averages of `Re ζᵏ` against `C_*(Π/π)` are `1, 0, 0, 0` for `k = 0, 1, 2, 3` (numerically to `10⁻¹²`), as for `dθ/2π`. Free spectral measure `μ = dx`, `β = 0`: `ν = σ`, so `klDiv σ σ = 0` (Mathlib `InformationTheory.klDiv_self`), and the formula gives `1 − 1 − (1/π)∫ log 1 dΠ = 0`.

tests.name: doubleLebesgueMassCorrection
tests.statement: `μ = 2 dx`, `β = 0`: `ν = 2σ`, `klDiv σ (2σ) = log(1/2) + 2 − 1 = 1 − log 2 ≈ 0.306853`, which the formula reproduces, and `S = log 2 = log ν(X)`: the equality case of the bound `klDiv σ ν ≥ ν(X) − 1 − log ν(X)` from `InformationTheory.mul_log_le_klDiv`. Reading `S` as `−klDiv σ ν`, without the mass correction, would give `log 2 − 1 ≈ −0.306853` instead.

tests.name: pointMassNotAbsolutelyContinuous
tests.statement: Point mass `μ = 0`, `β = 1`: `ν = δ₁` and `w = 0`. The set `X ∖ {1}` has `ν`-measure `0` and `σ`-measure `1`, so `σ` is not absolutely continuous with respect to `ν` and `klDiv σ δ₁ = ∞` (Mathlib `InformationTheory.klDiv_of_not_ac`), `S = −∞`. Two equal point masses, by contrast, give `klDiv δ₁ δ₁ = 0`, so this case needs the non-atomic first argument `σ`.

tests.name: junkValueOfLogarithm
tests.statement: Junk value of the logarithm: for `μ = w dx` with `w = 0` on `[0, 1]` and `w = 1` elsewhere, Mathlib's `Real.log 0 = 0` makes `log w` identically `0`, integrable with integral `0`, yet `σ` is not absolutely continuous with respect to `ν_{μ,0}` and `klDiv σ ν_{μ,0} = ∞`. The hypothesis `w > 0` almost everywhere is what separates the two cases.

tests.name: rectangularBarrier
tests.statement: Rectangular barrier `f = 0.7` on `[0, 1.3]`, the potential of §6.5's Checks, with `μ = dx/|E(T, x)|²`, `T = 1.3` and `β = 0`: `ν(X) = (1/π)∫ w dΠ = Im m(i) = 0.537539` (quadrature `0.537539`). Since `e^{iTz}E(T, z) = a(1 + ρ)` with `a` outer (§4.4) and `|ρ| < 1` (§4.3), `log|E(T, z)| − T Im z` is the Poisson integral of `log|E(T, ·)|`, so `(1/π)∫ log w dΠ = 2T − 2 log|E(T, i)| = −0.918466` (quadrature `−0.918467`). Hence `klDiv σ ν = 0.537539 − 1 + 0.918466 = 0.456005`, above the bound `ν(X) − 1 − log ν(X) = 0.158293`; a sign error in the transport would make it negative.

tests.name: semicontinuityIsNotContinuity
tests.statement: Semicontinuity is not continuity: `νₙ = (1 + sin nθ) dθ/2π = ν_{μₙ,0}` for `μₙ = (1 + sin(n arg C(x))) dx` converges weakly to `σ`, while `klDiv σ νₙ = −(1/2π)∫₀^{2π} log(1 + sin nθ) dθ = log 2 > 0 = klDiv σ σ` (numerically `0.693144` at `n = 3`), and the formula gives `1 − 1 − (−log 2)`. So the pinned lower semicontinuity cannot be improved to continuity.

targets.name: integrable_log_spectralDensity
targets.statement: Let `q` be square-integrable. Prove that `∫ log w dΠ ≥ −2π log 2 − π‖q‖²` and the same for `w̃`; hence `log w, log w̃ ∈ L¹(Π)` and `w, w̃ > 0` almost everywhere (poltoratski2024 line 263–268; mauth2022 Theorem 3 line 702–707; denisov2006 Theorem 11.1 line 3246 with the dictionary of §13). Route: for the truncation `q_T`, `w_T = |E(T, ·)|^{−2}` and `|E(T, x)| = |a(T, x) + b(T, x)| ≤ 2|a(T, x)|`, so `∫ log w_T dΠ ≥ −2π log 2 − 2∫ log|a(T, x)| dx = −2π log 2 − π‖q‖²_{L²(0,T)}` by §4.4. With `σ`, `ν_T = ν_{μ_T,0}` and `ν = ν_{μ_q,β}` as in §6.7, §6.7 gives `klDiv σ ν_T ≤ ν_T(X) − 1 + 2 log 2 + ‖q‖²`. The measures `ν_T` converge weakly to `ν` and `ν_T(X) → ν(X)` (truncation bullet of §6.5), and Tau Ceti `TauCeti.lowerSemicontinuous_klDiv_finiteMeasure`, with `σ` fixed, gives `klDiv σ ν ≤ ν(X) − 1 + 2 log 2 + ‖q‖² < ∞`. By §6.7, `w > 0` almost everywhere, `log w ∈ L¹(Π)` and `(1/π)∫ log w dΠ = ν(X) − 1 − klDiv σ ν ≥ −2 log 2 − ‖q‖²`. The Dirichlet side is the same with `|Ẽ(T, x)| = |a(T, x) − b(T, x)| ≤ 2|a(T, x)|`.

api.statement: Writing `E(x) = |E(x)| e^{−iψ(x)}` with `ψ` continuous on `ℝ`, so that `ψ = −arg E` (for `E = E(t, ·)` one may take `ψ = −φ(t, ·)`, the negative of the branch `φ` of §3.2), `θ_E(x) = e^{2iψ(x)}` and `ψ′(x) = π K(x, x)/|E(x)|² > 0`, with `K` the kernel of §6.1.

api.statement: If `(ζₙ)` are the zeros of `θ_E` in `ℂ₊` with multiplicity (the conjugates of the zeros of `E`), then `Σ Im ζₙ/(1 + |ζₙ|²) < ∞` and there is `c ≥ 0` with `2ψ′(x) = |θ_E′(x)| = c + Σₙ 2 Im ζₙ/|x − ζₙ|²` for every `x ∈ ℝ` (poltoratski2024 line 312–321 and the proof of Lemma 1, line 337–346).

api.name: routeHadamardFactorisationOf
api.statement: Route: Hadamard factorisation of `E` with genus one (AnalyticNumberTheoryPartI §0.23) gives `E′/E = β + Σₙ (1/(z − zₙ) + 1/zₙ)`; on `ℝ`, `θ_E′/θ_E = −2i Im(E′/E)`; the Hermite–Biehler inequality `|θ_E| ≤ 1` on `ℂ₊`, evaluated along `iy`, forces the Blaschke condition and `c ≥ 0`.

targets.name: tendsto_spectralDensity_mul_kernel_div_sinc
targets.statement: Prove that for almost every `s ∈ ℝ` and every `C > 0`, `sup_{λ ∈ Q(s, C/t)} |w(s) K_t(λ, λ)/Sinc_t(λ, λ) − 1| → 0` as `t → ∞`, where `K_t(λ, λ) = sup{|F(λ)|² : F ∈ PW_t, ∫|F|² dμ ≤ 1}` and `Sinc_t(λ, λ) = sup{|F(λ)|² : F ∈ PW_t, ∫|F|² dx ≤ 1} = sinh(2t Im λ)/(2π Im λ)` (poltoratski2024 Lemma 2 line 630–727; mauth2022 Lemma 21 line 794). Route (upper bound): let `G = O_{(1/2) log w}` be the outer function with `|G|² = w` on `ℝ` (§2.8; `log w ∈ L¹(Π)` by §6.8). Take `s` with `w(s) > 0` that is a Lebesgue point of `√(M_1 P[|log w|])` (§2.3) and at which `G` has a nontangential limit, and multiply `G` by a unimodular constant so that this limit is `√w(s)`. Almost every `s` qualifies: the limits exist almost everywhere by the boundary-value bullet of §2.8, because `w dx ≤ μ` is Poisson-finite. Rescale by `t`: `G_t(z) = G(s + z/t)` is outer with boundary modulus `√w(s + ·/t)`, by the covariance of §2.1 and the characterisation of §2.8. A counterexample sequence `fₙ ∈ PW_1` with `∫ |fₙ|² w(s + ·/kₙ) dx ≤ 1` has `e^{iz}fₙ ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` (§2.7). So `e^{iz}fₙ G_{kₙ} ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` with norm at most `1`, by the outer-multiplier bullet of §2.8. A subsequence converges weakly and normally (§2.6), and §2.7's characterisation produces an `H ∈ PW_1` violating the extremal value. Lower bound: `|Sinc(t, λ, ·)|²/‖Sinc(t, λ, ·)‖²₂` is an approximate identity at `s`, so its `μ`-integral tends to `w(s)` at almost every `s` (§2.4), and `Sinc(t, λ, ·)/‖·‖_μ` is a competitor.

tests.statement: For real `λ`, `Sinc_t(λ, λ) = t/π`, so the statement says `K_t(λ, λ) = (t/π)(1/w(s) + o(1))` uniformly for `|λ − s| ≤ C/t`.

targets.name: kernel_sub_sinc_isLittleO
targets.statement: Prove that for almost every `s` and every `C > 0`, `sup_{λ, z ∈ Q(s, C/t)} |K(t, λ, z) − Sinc(t, λ, z)/w(s)| = o(t)` (poltoratski2024 Lemma 4 (6.6) line 756–792; mauth2022 Lemma 22 line 1129). Route: `Δ = K(t, λ_t, ·) − Sinc(t, λ_t, ·)/w(s)` lies in `PW_t` (§6.2, §2.7), so `e^{itz}Δ ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` (§2.7). Since `w dx ≤ μ`, §8.3 gives `∫ |Δ|² w dx ≤ ∫ |Δ|² dμ = o(t)`. Let `G = O_{(1/2) log w}` be the outer function with `|G|² = w` on `ℝ` (§2.8, §6.8). The outer-multiplier bullet of §2.8 then gives `F(t, ·) = e^{itz} G Δ ∈ H²(ℂ₊)` with `‖F(t, ·)‖² = ∫ |Δ|² w dx = o(t)`. Hence `F(t, ·)` has nontangential maximal function `o(√t)` in `L²` (§2.6); choose two real points on either side of `Q(s, C/t)` where it is `o(t)` and where `√(M_1 P[log w])` is controlled; the difference of kernels is real entire, so the bound on the boundary of a rhombus symmetric about `ℝ` gives the bound inside by the maximum principle.

Route: `E(t, z(t)) = 0` gives `A(t, z(t)) = iC(t, z(t)) = β`, so `D(t, ·, z(t)) = iβE(t, ·)`, since `D(t, λ, z(t)) = βC(t, λ) + iβA(t, λ)`, and §8.5 makes `iβE` close to `sin(t(· − z(t)))/w(s)`; the determinant identity (2.2) at two points fixes `2|β|²w(s) = (1 + o(1)) sinh(2t y(t))`.

targets.statement: Prove (poltoratski2024 Corollary 3 line 1002–1012 and the argument of line 918–996; mauth2022 Corollary 6 line 1397–1408): (1) for almost every `s` there are `C(t) → ∞` and `z(t) = x(t) − iy(t) ∈ ℂ₋` with `sup_{z ∈ Q(s, C(t)/t)} |E(t, z) − α(s, t) γ(t y(t)) sin(t(z − z(t)))/√w(s)| → 0` as `t → ∞` in `T₁(s, C)`, `|α| = 1`, where `z(t)` is a zero of `E(t, ·)` when `t ∈ T₀(s, C)`, and the same function `C(t)` gives the approximation of `Ẽ(t, ·)` of this form, with `w̃(s)`, `T̃₀(s, C)` and `T̃₁(s, C)` in place of `w(s)`, `T₀(s, C)` and `T₁(s, C)`; (2) if the approximation of `E` in (1) holds at `s` for a function `C(t) → ∞` and `t ∉ T₀(s, C(t))` for all large `t`, then for every `D > 0`, `sup_{z ∈ Q(s, D/t)} |E(t, z) + iα(s, t) e^{−itz}/√w(s)| → 0`; (3) for almost every `s`: if `T₀(s, K)` is bounded for every `K > 0`, then for every `D > 0` there are unimodular `α(s, t)` with `sup_{z ∈ Q(s, D/t)} |E(t, z) + iα(s, t) e^{−itz}/√w(s)| → 0` as `t → ∞`. Route: §8.5 with two values of the second argument shows that `(A(t, x), C(t, x))` has modulus bounded below and rotates on `ℝ ∩ Q(s, C/t)`; choosing `x₀`, `x₁` with `C(t, x₀) = 0 < A(t, x₀) = c₁` and `A(t, x₁) = 0 < C(t, x₁) = c₂`, and `x₂ = x₁ − π/(2t)`, gives `C(t, z) ≈ sin(t(z − x₀))/(c₁w)`, `A(t, z) ≈ cos(t(z − x₂))/(c₂w)`, so `E ≈ cos(t(z − x₂))/(c₂w) − i sin(t(z − x₀))/(c₁w)`, with `c₁c₂w = cos(t(x₂ − x₀)) + o(1)`; if `t(x₂ − x₀)` were not `o(1)` modulo `2π`, or `c₁ − c₂` not `o(1)`, the phase derivative of `E` would vary by a factor `1 + ε` on an interval of length `8π/t`, and §7.2 would give a zero in `Q(s, C/t)`. For `Ẽ = B − iD` the same argument runs with `B`, `D`, `μ̃` and `w̃` in place of `A`, `C`, `μ` and `w`; one function serves `E` and `Ẽ` because the functions of §8.5 and §8.6 come from diagonal arguments over constant box sizes (poltoratski2024 line 832–833, 879 and 907–909), which can be run for the two at once. Route of (3), with constant boxes: at an `s` where §8.5 holds and `w(s) > 0`, fix `δ > 0`, let `ε > 0` be such that every two-term form allowed by the route (`c₁`, `c₂` within the bounds it gives and `c₁c₂w = cos(t(x₂ − x₀))`, so that `cos(t(x₂ − x₀))` is bounded below by a positive constant) whose parameters are `δ`-far from `t(x₂ − x₀) ∈ 2πℤ`, `c₁ = c₂` has phase derivative varying by a factor more than `1 + 2ε` on `J_t = (s − 4π/t, s + 4π/t)`, and take `K ≥ max(D, 4π + 24π/ε)`. For large `t` the box `Q(s, K/t)` contains no zero of `E(t, ·)` and §8.5 on it gives the two-term form there; a phase derivative of `E` varying by the factor `1 + ε` on `J_t` would give, by §7.2, a zero within `24π/(εt)` of `J_t`, hence in `Q(s, K/t)`. So the parameters are `δ`-close, `E` is within `O(δe^D) + o(1)` of `e^{itx₀} e^{−itz}/√w(s)` on `Q(s, D/t)`, and `δ` is arbitrary: `α = ie^{itx₀}`.

targets.name: diracE_exact_form_at_point
targets.statement: Let `s ∈ ℝ`, let `w, w̃ > 0` be numbers and let `C > 1`. Prove that there are `ε₀ > 0` and `D`, depending only on `C`, `w` and `w̃`, with the following property. Let `t > 0` and let `E`, `Ẽ` be entire functions with `E(s) conj Ẽ(s) − Ẽ(s) conj E(s) = 2i`, the determinant identity (2.2) of §3.2 at the real point `s`. Suppose that for some `0 < ε < ε₀`, some `x, x̃, y ∈ ℝ` with `1 < ty < 2C`, `−π/2 < t(x̃ − x) < π/2` and `cos(t(x̃ − x)) = √(w w̃)`, and some unimodular `α`, both `sup_{z ∈ Q(s, 3C/t)} |E(z) − α γ(ty) sin(t(z − (x − iy)))/√w| < ε` and `sup_{z ∈ Q(s, 3C/t)} |Ẽ(z) − α γ(ty) cos(t(z − (x̃ − iy)))/√w̃| < ε`. Then there are `x′, x̃′, y′ ∈ ℝ` and a unimodular `α′` with `|tx′ − tx| + |tx̃′ − tx̃| + |ty′ − ty| + |α′ − α| < Dε`, `x̃′ − x′ = x̃ − x`, and exactly `E(s) = α′ γ(ty′) sin(t(s − (x′ − iy′)))/√w` and `Ẽ(s) = α′ γ(ty′) cos(t(s − (x̃′ − iy′)))/√w̃` (poltoratski2024 Lemma 8 line 1116–1172 and mauth2022 Lemma 45 line 3251–3298, which print the factor `γ(ty)` in (8.5) and (58); the third Check shows that (2.2) forces `γ(ty′)`). §9.3 applies it to `E = E(t, ·)` and `Ẽ = Ẽ(t, ·)`, which satisfy (2.2) on `ℝ` (§3.2), at the points `p` of `ℝ ∩ Q(s, C/2ⁿ⁺¹)`, keeping the numbers `w = w(s)` and `w̃ = w̃(s)`, for the points `s` where `w(s) w̃(s) > 0`, which are almost all `s` by §6.8. Route: the quotient `g(z) = sin(t(z − (x − iy)))/cos(t(z − (x̃ − iy)))` has `g′(z) = t cos(t(x̃ − x))/cos²(t(z − (x̃ − iy)))`, of modulus at least `t √(w w̃)/cosh²(5C)` on `Q(s, 3C/t)`, so it attains the value `√(w/w̃) E(s)/Ẽ(s)` at a point `a` with `|a − s| ≤ D₂ε/t` (on the disc of radius `c/t` about `s`, with `c` depending only on `C`, `w`, `w̃`, `|g′ − g′(s)| ≤ |g′(s)|/2` because `|g″| ≲ t²` there, so `g` maps the disc of radius `r ≤ c/t` about `s` onto a set containing the disc of radius `|g′(s)| r/2` about `g(s)`, and the value is within `O(ε)` of `g(s)`); put `x′ = x − Re(a − s)`, `x̃′ = x̃ − Re(a − s)` and `y′ = y + Im(a − s)`. Then `E(s) = κ sin(t(s − (x′ − iy′)))/√w` and `Ẽ(s) = κ cos(t(s − (x̃′ − iy′)))/√w̃` for one `κ ∈ ℂ`, and (2.2) at `s` gives `|κ|² sinh(2ty′) = 2`, that is `|κ| = γ(ty′)`.
hypotheses: s ∈ ℝ, w, w̃ > 0 numbers, C > 1
E, Ẽ entire with E(s) conj Ẽ(s) − Ẽ(s) conj E(s) = 2i
the two approximations on Q(s,3C/t) with error ε < ε₀
