tests.name: ifTheApproximationsAre
tests.statement: If the approximations are exact at `s`, the conclusion holds with `x′ = x`, `x̃′ = x̃`, `y′ = y`, `α′ = α`.

tests.name: theConstraintKeepsThe
tests.statement: The constraint `1 < ty < 2C` keeps the quotient holomorphic near `s` (no zero of the cosine within `1/(2t)` of `ℝ ∩ Q(s, 3C/t)`).

tests.name: moduliFixTheFactor
tests.statement: Moduli: two forms `κ sin(t(s − (x′ − iy′)))/√w` and `κ cos(t(s − (x̃′ − iy′)))/√w̃` with `cos(t(x̃′ − x′)) = √(w w̃)` have determinant `E conj Ẽ − Ẽ conj E = i|κ|² sinh(2ty′)` at the real point `s`, so (2.2) fixes `|κ| = γ(ty′)`. With the factor `γ(ty)` printed in the sources and `y′ ≠ y` it is `2i sinh(2ty′)/sinh(2ty)`, not `2i`: for `w = 0.7`, `w̃ = 0.9`, `t = 1`, `s = 0`, `ty = 1.5` it is `2.0820i` at `ty′ = 1.52` and `2.4448i` at `ty′ = 1.6`, while the factor `γ(ty′)` gives `2i` in both cases.

tests.name: sourceFactorCannotBeKept
tests.statement: The factor `γ(ty)` cannot be kept: with it, (2.2) forces `y′ = y`, and only `x′` and `arg α′` remain to match the three real parameters of `(E(s), Ẽ(s))`. In the setting of the previous Check take for `E(s)`, `Ẽ(s)` the forms with `x = 0.3`, height `1.52` and factor `γ(1.52)`; they satisfy (2.2) and differ by `0.0023` and `0.0020` from the forms with `x = 0.3`, height `1.5` and factor `γ(1.5)`. The conclusion holds exactly with `x′ = 0.3`, `y′ = 1.52`, `α′ = 1`, whereas at height `1.5` with factor `γ(1.5)` no real `x′` matches both moduli (the larger of the two modulus errors is at least `0.0012`).

layers.title: Pointwise convergence of the non-linear Fourier transform

targets.name: intervalScattering
targets.statement: For `0 ≤ t₁ ≤ t₂` define the transfer matrix `M_{t₁→t₂} = M(t₂, ·) M(t₁, ·)^{−1}` and its Hermite–Biehler and scattering functions `E_{t₁→t₂}`, `Ẽ_{t₁→t₂}`, `a_{t₁→t₂}`, `b_{t₁→t₂}` as those of the potential `f(t₁ + ·) 1_{[0, t₂ − t₁]}` at time `t₂ − t₁` (poltoratski2024 line 1183–1210). Its API:

api.name: isTheFundamentalMatrix
api.statement: `M_{t₁→t₂}` is the fundamental matrix of `f(t₁ + ·)` at time `t₂ − t₁` (§3.1 chain rule).

api.name: andPoltoratskiLine
api.statement: `a_{t₁→t₂} = e^{i(t₂−t₁)z}(E(t₂)Ẽ#(t₁) − Ẽ(t₂)E#(t₁))/(2i)` and `b_{t₁→t₂} = e^{i(t₂−t₁)z}(Ẽ(t₂)E(t₁) − E(t₂)Ẽ(t₁))/(2i)` (poltoratski2024 (9.1)–(9.3) line 1228–1319).

api.name: poltoratskiLine
api.statement: `∫ log|a_{t₁→t₂}(x)| dx = (π/2) ∫_{t₁}^{t₂} f²` (§4.4; poltoratski2024 line 1209–1210).

api.name: theNonLinearFourier
api.statement: The non-linear Fourier transform of `f 1_{(t₁, t₂)}` is `e^{2izt₁} b_{t₁→t₂}/a_{t₁→t₂}` (§5.6 translation).

tests.name: andTheFormulasReduce
tests.statement: `t₁ = 0`: `E(0) = 1`, `Ẽ(0) = −i`, and the formulas reduce to `a = e^{it₂z}(E + iẼ)/2`, `b = e^{it₂z}(E − iẼ)/2`.

tests.name: freeCase
tests.statement: Free case: `a_{t₁→t₂} = 1`, `b_{t₁→t₂} = 0`.

targets.name: intervalScattering_trig_eval
targets.statement: Let `s ∈ ℝ`, `w, w̃ > 0` with `w w̃ ≤ 1`, `Φ ∈ (−π/2, π/2)` with `cos Φ = √(w w̃)`, and for `k = 1, 2` let `t_k > 0`, `x_k ∈ ℝ`, `y_k > 0`, `|α_k| = 1` with `E(t_k, s) = α_k γ(t_k y_k) sin θ_k/√w` and `Ẽ(t_k, s) = α_k γ(t_k y_k) cos(θ_k − Φ)/√w̃`, where `θ_k = t_k(s − x_k + iy_k)`. Put `υ = t₁y₁`, `e = ε₁ + iε₂` with `ε₁ = t₂(s − x₂) − t₁(s − x₁)`, `ε₂ = t₂y₂ − t₁y₁`, and `N = (sinh 2υ sinh 2(υ + ε₂))^{1/2}`. Prove the exact identities `a_{t₁→t₂}(s) = e^{i(t₂−t₁)s} α₂ conj(α₁) sin(e + 2iυ)/(iN)`, `b_{t₁→t₂}(s) = −e^{i(t₂−t₁)s} α₂ α₁ sin(e)/(iN)`, and hence `(f 1_{(t₁,t₂)})⌃(s) = −e^{2ist₁} α₁² sin e/sin(e + 2iυ)` (poltoratski2024 (9.2), (9.4) and line 1253–1347). Route: `sin A cos(B − Φ) − cos(A − Φ) sin B = cos Φ sin(A − B)` with `A = θ₂`, `B = conj θ₁` (and the analogous identity for `b`), and `γ(p)γ(p′) = 2/(sinh 2p sinh 2p′)^{1/2}`.
hypotheses: E(t_k,s), Ẽ(t_k,s) of the stated sin/cos forms, k = 1, 2

tests.name: asSuRequiresOn
tests.statement: `|a|² − |b|² = (sinh²(ε₂ + 2υ) − sinh² ε₂)/N² = 1`, as SU(1,1) requires on `ℝ`; numerically, for `w = 0.7`, `w̃ = 0.9`, `s = 0.3`, `(t₁, x₁, y₁) = (50, 0.31, 0.03)`, `(t₂, x₂, y₂) = (60, 0.305, 0.025)`, the direct and closed forms agree to `10^{−15}` and `|a|² − |b|² = 1.0000000000`.

tests.name: theDataAtA
tests.statement: The data at a single time satisfy (2.2): `E Ẽ# − Ẽ E# = 2i` at `s` exactly when `cos Φ = √(w w̃)`.

tests.name: andNoMotionOf
tests.statement: `e = 0`: `b = 0` and `|a| = sinh 2υ/N = 1`; no motion of the resonance means no scattering at `s`.

targets.name: resonance_time_proportion_tendsto_zero
targets.statement: Prove that for almost every `s` and every `C > 0`, if `Iₙ(s)` is the longest subinterval of `[2ⁿ, 2ⁿ⁺¹]` such that `Q(s, C/t)` contains a zero of `E(t, ·)` for every `t ∈ Iₙ(s)`, then `|Iₙ(s)|/2ⁿ → 0` (poltoratski2024 Lemma 9 line 1350–1377; mauth2022 §3.3 Corollary 7 line 1525 for the analogous half-line statement). Route: if the set of `s` with `lim sup |Iₙ(s)|/2ⁿ > 2/m` had positive measure, then for infinitely many `n` a set `Sₙ` of measure `≳ |Zₙ|/m`, `Zₙ = {s : |Iₙ(s)| > 2ⁿ/m}`, shares a time `t₁` in the middle thirds of the `Iₙ(s)`; put `t₂ = t₁ + 2ⁿ/(3m)` and `J(s) = ℝ ∩ Q(s, C/2ⁿ⁺¹)`, an interval of length `C/2ⁿ`, for `s ∈ Sₙ`. §8.8, with §8.9 applied at each `p ∈ J(s)` to the numbers `w(s)`, `w̃(s)`, puts the data at `p` in the form of §9.2 with increment `e(p) = e(s) + (t₂ − t₁)(p − s) + o(1)`, whose real part sweeps an interval of length `C/(3m)` as `p` runs over `J(s)`. There `|a_{t₁→t₂}(p)|² = 1 + (sin² Re e(p) + sinh² Im e(p))/N²`, with `N` bounded in terms of `C` because the resonances at `t₁` and `t₂` lie in their boxes; so `∫_{J(s)} log|a_{t₁→t₂}| ≥ c_{m,C} |J(s)|` with `c_{m,C} > 0`, although the integrand vanishes where `e(p) = 0`. Since `log|a_{t₁→t₂}| ≥ 0` on `ℝ` (§4.3), a cover of `Sₙ` of index two by the `J(s)` and §9.1's Plancherel identity give `|Zₙ| ≲_{m,C} ‖f‖²_{L²(2ⁿ, 2ⁿ⁺¹)}`, which is summable, and Borel–Cantelli concludes.

tests.name: compactSupportTheResonances
tests.statement: Compact support: the resonances are fixed (§8 Examples), so `Iₙ(s) = ∅` for large `n`.

tests.name: summabilityInput
tests.statement: Summability input: `Σₙ ‖f‖²_{L²(2ⁿ, 2ⁿ⁺¹)} = ‖f‖²_{L²(1, ∞)} < ∞`.

tests.name: aResonanceAtFixed
tests.statement: A resonance at fixed distance `δ` from `s` lies in `Q(s, C/t)` only for `t ≤ C/δ`, so it contributes to `Iₙ(s)` only for `2ⁿ ≤ C/δ`.

tests.name: integralBoundNotPointwise
tests.statement: The lower bound is for the integral only. With `υ = 1`, `Im e = 0` and `e(s) = 0`, the formula of §9.2 gives `log|a_{t₁→t₂}| = ½ log(1 + sin²(Re e)/sinh² 2)`: `0` at `p = s` and `≈ 0.000379` at the shift `Re e = 0.1`, with mean `≈ 0.000126 > 0` over shifts in `[−0.1, 0.1]`. A pointwise bound `log|a_{t₁→t₂}| ≥ c > 0` on `J(s)` fails at `p = s`.

targets.name: resonanceFreePoints
targets.statement: Call `s ∈ ℝ` a resonance-free point of the real potential `f` when, for every `C > 0`, the sets of times `T₀(s, C)` and `T̃₀(s, C)` of §8.1 are bounded: there is `T(s, C)` such that `Q(s, C/t)` contains no zero of `E(t, ·)` and no zero of `Ẽ(t, ·)` for `t > T(s, C)`. Write `R(f)` for the set of resonance-free points (poltoratski2024 line 97–101 and 1173–1176, where the condition for `E` at almost every point is the property from which Theorem 1 is deduced; mauth2022 line 1893–1894, whose exceptional set `{s : T₀(s, C) is unbounded}` is the complement of the condition for `E` at one `C`). Its API:

api.name: forThereIsSuch
api.statement: For `s ∈ R(f)` there is `C(t) → ∞` such that `Q(s, C(t)/t)` contains no zero of `E(t, ·)` or of `Ẽ(t, ·)` for all large `t`: with `T_k = max(k, T(s, 1), …, T(s, k))`, put `C(t) = k` for `T_k < t ≤ T_{k+1}`.

api.name: conjugatingTheSystemBy
api.statement: Conjugating the system by `Ω` changes the sign of the potential: `M_{−f}(t, z) = Ω M_f(t, z) Ω⁻¹`, that is `A_{−f} = D_f`, `C_{−f} = −B_f`, `B_{−f} = −C_f`, `D_{−f} = A_f`. Hence `Ẽ_f(t, ·) = −i E_{−f}(t, ·)` and `Ẽ_{−f}(t, ·) = −i E_f(t, ·)`, so `R(f) = R(−f)`; the Weyl function of `−f` is `−1/m_f`, so the density `w_{−f}` of §6.5 is the Dirichlet density `w̃_f`.

api.name: ifVanishesOnThen
api.statement: If `f` vanishes on `[T₀, ∞)` for some `T₀ > 0`, then `R(f) = ℝ`: for `t ≥ T₀`, `E(t, ·) = e^{−i(t−T₀)z} E(T₀, ·)` and `Ẽ(t, ·) = e^{−i(t−T₀)z} Ẽ(T₀, ·)` (the free equation), whose zeros are the fixed zeros of `E(T₀, ·)` and `Ẽ(T₀, ·)`, all in the open lower half-plane (§3.3); the finitely many in the compact box `Q(s, C/T₀)`, which contains `Q(s, C/t)` for `t ≥ T₀`, lie at a distance at least some `δ > 0` from `ℝ`, so `Q(s, C/t)`, where `|Im z| ≤ C/t`, contains none of them for `t > max(T₀, C/δ)`.

tests.name: freeCaseAndHave
tests.statement: Free case: `E(t, ·) = e^{−itz}` and `Ẽ(t, ·) = −i e^{−itz}` have no zeros, so `R(0) = ℝ`.

tests.name: hasInfinitelyManyZeros
tests.statement: `f = c 1_{[0,T₀]}`: `E(t, ·)` has infinitely many zeros for every `t ≥ T₀` (§7 Examples), and still `R(f) = ℝ` by the third bullet; the condition concerns boxes of size `C/t` about `s`, not the absence of zeros.

tests.name: notSquareIntegrableWith
tests.statement: `f ≡ c > 0` (not square-integrable). With `κ = √(c² − z²)`, `E(t, z) = cosh κt + (c − iz) sinh κt/κ` and `Ẽ(t, z) = −i(cosh κt − (c + iz) sinh κt/κ)`; a zero of `E(t, ·)` needs `e^{2κt} = (c − iz − κ)/(c − iz + κ)` and a zero of `Ẽ(t, ·)` needs `e^{2κt} = (c + iz + κ)/(c + iz − κ)`. For `0 < |s| < c` both right sides stay bounded on `Q(s, C/t)` while `|e^{2κt}|` grows like `e^{2√(c² − s²)t}`, so `s ∈ R(f)`. At `s = 0` the second denominator vanishes and `Ẽ(t, ·)` has a zero near `−2ic e^{−2ct}` (for `c = 1`, `t = 5`: `−9.0808·10⁻⁵ i`, against `−9.0800·10⁻⁵ i`), so `0 ∉ R(f)`, while `E(t, ·)` has no zero near `0`: a definition through `E` alone would admit `0`. At `s = 1/2` (`c = 1`) the point is resonance-free while `|E(10, 1/2)| ≈ 6434` grows like `e^{(√3/2)t}`, so resonance-freeness alone does not give the conclusions of §9.5, which also need square integrability.

tests.name: membershipInIsNot
tests.statement: Membership in `R(f)` is not decided by the moduli at `s` of the transforms of `f` on subintervals. For data in the forms of §9.2 at times `t_j < t_k`, `|(f 1_{(t_j,t_k)})⌃(s)| = |sin(θ_k − θ_j)/sin(θ_k − conj θ_j)|`, which is the pseudo-hyperbolic distance `|ζ_k − ζ_j|/|1 − conj ζ_j ζ_k|` of the points `ζ_k = e^{2iθ_k}` of the unit disc and is unchanged by every automorphism of the disc; inserting a zero interval of length `β` after `t₁` replaces the restriction of `f` to each subinterval by a translate, whose transform has the same modulus at `s` (§5.6). With `θ_k = i h_k`, the heights `1, 0.99, 0.98` (a resonance moving towards `ℝ`) and `1, 1.0102119, 1.0208659` (its image under the half-turn of the disc about `ζ₁`, a resonance moving away) give the same moduli `d₁₂ = 0.0027860`, `d₂₃ = 0.0028445`, `d₁₃ = 0.0056305` on `(t₁, t₂)`, `(t₂, t₃)`, `(t₁, t₃)`, and in both cases `d₁₃ = (d₁₂ + d₂₃)/(1 + d₁₂ d₂₃)`, the addition law of pseudo-hyperbolic distances along a geodesic.

targets.name: diracE_asymptotics_resonanceFree
targets.statement: Prove that for every real square-integrable `f` there is a Lebesgue-null set `N_f` such that for every `s ∈ R(f) ∖ N_f` and every `D > 0` there are unimodular `α(s, t)` and a constant `β(s)` with `Im β(s) = −√(w(s) w̃(s))`, `|β(s)| = 1`, such that `sup_{Q(s,D/t)} |E(t, z) + iα(s, t) e^{−itz}/√w(s)| → 0` and `sup_{Q(s,D/t)} |Ẽ(t, z) + iβ(s) α(s, t) e^{−itz}/√w̃(s)| → 0`; consequently `|E(t, s)| → 1/√w(s)`, `|Ẽ(t, s)| → 1/√w̃(s)`, `|a(t, s)|² → (1/w + 1/w̃ + 2)/4` and `|b(t, s)|² → (1/w + 1/w̃ − 2)/4` at `s` (poltoratski2024 (9.9)–(9.10) line 1538–1574; mauth2022 line 3855–3875). Route: `N_f` is the union of the exceptional null sets of §8.7(3) for `f` and for `−f` and of `{w w̃ = 0}` (§6.8). At `s ∈ R(f) ∖ N_f` the sets `T₀(s, K)` are bounded for every `K > 0` (§9.4), so §8.7(3) gives the approximation of `E`; and §8.7(3) for `−f`, whose sets `T₀(s, K)` are the sets `T̃₀(s, K)` of `f` because `E_{−f} = iẼ_f`, with `w_{−f} = w̃_f` (§9.4), gives that of `Ẽ`. The determinant identity (2.2) on `ℝ` gives `(conj β − β)/√(w w̃) = 2i`, and continuity of `Ẽ(t, s)/E(t, s)` in `t` makes `β` constant.
hypotheses: s ∈ R(f) outside a null set N_f, D > 0

tests.name: inTheLimitBy
tests.statement: `|b|² ≥ 0` in the limit: `1/w + 1/w̃ ≥ 2/√(w w̃) ≥ 2` by the arithmetic–geometric mean inequality and `w w̃ ≤ 1` (§6.5); and `|a|² − |b|² → 1`.

tests.name: compactSupportAtFor
tests.statement: Compact support at `x = 0` for `f = c 1_{[0,T]}`, where `R(f) = ℝ` (§9.4): `w(0) = e^{−2cT}`, `w̃(0) = e^{2cT}`, and the limit `|a|² = (e^{2cT} + e^{−2cT} + 2)/4 = cosh² cT` is the exact value `a(T, 0) = cosh cT`.

targets.name: nlft_truncate_tendsto_resonanceFree
targets.statement: Prove that for every real square-integrable `f` there is a Lebesgue-null set `N′_f` containing the set `N_f` of §9.5 such that for every `s ∈ R(f) ∖ N′_f`: `b(T, s)/a(T, s) = (f_T)⌃*(s) → f⌃*(s)` as `T → ∞`; the strong form holds, `sup_{|z − s| < C/T} |(f_T)⌃(z) − f⌃*(s)| → 0` for every `C > 0`, where `(f_T)⌃ = b(T, ·)/a(T, ·)` is holomorphic on the disc for large `T`; the moduli `|a(T, s)|` and `|b(T, s)|` converge; and the generalised eigenfunction `t ↦ M(t, s)` is bounded on `[0, ∞)` (poltoratski2024 Theorem 1 line 578–586, line 54–57 and the deduction (9.9)–(9.10) line 1538–1582; mauth2022 Theorem 2 line 216 and its deduction at line 3851–3862; both deduce the theorem from the resonance-free condition at almost every point). Route: §9.5 makes `b/a = (E − iẼ)/(E + iẼ)` uniformly close on `Q(s, D/T)` to the constant `(1/√w − iβ/√w̃)/(1/√w + iβ/√w̃)`, whose denominator has squared modulus `1/w + 1/w̃ + 2 > 0`, so the limit exists at every `s ∈ R(f) ∖ N_f`; §5.5 gives `(f_T)⌃* → f⌃*` in `Π`-measure, so along a sequence `T_k → ∞` almost everywhere, and `N′_f` adds to `N_f` the null set where this fails; `|A|, |C| ≤ |E|` and `|B|, |D| ≤ |Ẽ|` on `ℝ` bound `M(t, s)`.
hypotheses: s ∈ R(f) outside a null set N′_f ⊇ N_f

locator.where: Theorem 1 line 578–586, line 54–57 and (9.9)–(9.10) line 1538–1582; mauth2022 Theorem 2 line 216 and line 3851–3862

tests.name: integrableByTheConvergence
tests.statement: `f` integrable: by §5.2 the convergence holds uniformly on `ℝ`, at every point, resonance-free or not; on `R(f) ∖ N′_f` the two statements agree.

tests.name: compactSupportAndFor
tests.statement: Compact support: `R(f) = ℝ` (§9.4) and `(f_T)⌃* = f⌃*` for `T ≥ T₀`, so the convergence holds at every `s`.

tests.name: squareIntegrabilityCannotBe
